stories.title: Lakers honor longtime PA announcer Lawrence Tanter
stories.summary: The Los Angeles Lakers honored longtime public address announcer Lawrence Tanter by unveiling a plaque at Crypto.com Arena on Monday, Nov. 23.
stories.detailText: The Los Angeles Lakers honored longtime public address announcer Lawrence Tanter by unveiling a plaque at Crypto.com Arena on Monday, Nov. 23. Tanter spent 43 seasons in that role for the franchise before his death at 76 on Sept. 23 . Tanter had officially retired in June. He had called more than 2,100 games, including 14 NBA Finals series and four NBA All-Star Games, during his tenure. The Lakers played a tribute video during the game that included remarks from Lakers legends Michael Cooper and Mychal Thompson. Fans were also given the opportunity to write messages and memories in honor of Tanter in the Star Plaza outside of the Lakers’ home arena. Lakers coach JJ Redick also shared some thoughts about Tanter before the game against the Utah Jazz on Monday. "He's an iconic voice," Redick told reporters. "He made a mark not only on the Lakers but the NBA." “The first time I ever got to play in Staples Center, the curtains dropped from the scoreboard and the music came on and you hear his voice. … It just felt like I made the NBA. He was an integral part of what made this place so special.” This article originally appeared on USA TODAY: Lakers honor longtime PA announcer Lawrence Tanter

stories.summary: The Lakers honored Lawrence Tanter with a video tribute on Monday as the Lakers played the Jazz. The video included footage of Tanter introducing Magic Johnson, Kareem Abdul-Jabbar, Shaquille O’Neal,...
stories.detailText: The Lakers honored Lawrence Tanter with a video tribute on Monday as the Lakers played the Jazz. The video included footage of Tanter introducing Magic Johnson, Kareem Abdul-Jabbar, Shaquille O’Neal, Kobe Bryant, LeBron James and Luka Doncic, as well as his signature “Laker girl” call and a banner drop over his 43 years as the team’s P.A. announcer. Former Lakers Mychal Thompson and Michael Cooper then took the court to say a few words about Tanter, who died at age 76 in September . Mychal Thompson, left, and Michael Cooper honor the late Lawrence Tanter during a game between the Lakers and Jazz on Monday, Nov. 23, 2026, in Los Angeles. Getty Images “As much as you guys love him, we love him even more,” said Thompson, who won two championships with the Lakers in 1987 and 1988 as Tanter served as the team’s P.A. announcer. Tanter was the voice of the Lakers during 10 NBA championships after being hired during the 1982-83 season. The Los Angeles Lakers honor Lawrence Tanter outside Crypto.Com Arena on Monday, Nov. 23, 2026, in Los Angeles, before a game against the Utah Jazz. NBAE via Getty Images The Lakers also honored Tanter with a commemorative banner on Star Plaza outside of Crypto.com Arena before Monday’s game. Fans were able to share personal messages and memories from 4 p.m. to 8 p.m. Tanter suffered a a stroke in March before moving into an advisory role in June. The Los Angeles Lakers honor Lawrence Tanter outside of Crypto.Com Arena before a game against the Utah Jazz in Los Angeles on Monday, Nov. 23, 2026. NBAE via Getty Images “We are deeply saddened to share the news of the passing of legendary Lakers public address announcer Lawrence Tanter,” the Lakers said in a statement in September . “For 43 years, LT’s voice served as the soundtrack to Lakers games at the arena. He will be remembered as a cherished member of the Lakers family.”

stories.title: Jalen Green scores 25 and Devin Booker adds 22 to help the Suns top the Pelicans 123-119 in OT
stories.summary: — Jalen Green scored 25 points, Devin Booker added 22, and the Phoenix Suns defeated the New Orleans Pelicans, 123-119 in overtime on Monday night.
stories.detailText: NEW ORLEANS -- — Jalen Green scored 25 points, Devin Booker added 22, and the Phoenix Suns defeated the New Orleans Pelicans , 123-119 in overtime on Monday night. Collin Gillespie scored five of his 18 points in overtime, and Miles Bridges had 13 points and 11 rebounds for Phoenix, which won its fourth straight game while handing New Orleans its fourth straight loss. Jordan Poole scored 28 points — all in the first three quarters — and Zion Williamson added 25 points for the Pelicans, who've dropped 10 of 11 since starting 4-4. Saddiq Bey added 21 points and Jeremiah Fears had 11 assists for New Orleans. But Fears, who'd scored 29 points in a loss at San Antonio on Saturday, missed 14 of 17 shots against Phoenix. Trey Murphy also struggled as he works his way back from knee soreness that had sidelined him for seven of New Orleans' previous eight games. He shot 4 of 14 from the floor, and 1 of 6 from 3-point range. The Suns pulled away for good with a 10-4 run during overtime that included Booker's jumper, Gillespie's layup as he was fouled and Bridges' 3. Phoenix also led 109-107 with 31 seconds left in regulation after Booker's step-back jumper. Fears' driving scoop tied it at 109 with 22.8 seconds left, and Herb Jones' steal of Booker's pass in the final seconds of the fourth quarter forced overtime. Poole, who scored 25 points two nights earlier in San Antonio, made his first nine shots against Phoenix, including six from 3-point range. He scored 17 in the first half, after which Phoenix led 56-54. Derik Queen scored 11 points for the Pelicans, but missed four of five free throws in the fourth quarter, when the Pelicans missed six of 12 from the line. Up next Suns: At Houston in NBA Cup West Group A play on Wednesday. Pelicans: At Los Angeles Clippers in NBA Cup West Group B play on Friday. ------ See AP’s full NBA coverage here

stories.title: Kevin Durant scores 32 to power Rockets past Clippers 116-104
stories.summary: — Kevin Durant scored 32 points and Alperen Sengun and Amen Thompson each had 20 to lead the Houston Rockets to a 116-104 win over the Los Angeles Clippers on Monday night.
stories.detailText: HOUSTON -- — Kevin Durant scored 32 points and Alperen Sengun and Amen Thompson each had 20 to lead the Houston Rockets to a 116-104 win over the Los Angeles Clippers on Monday night. Houston led by six points with about three minutes remaining before Durant made consecutive 3-pointers to make it 109-97. Brandon Ingram made a basket for Los Angeles but an off-balance 3 by Durant seconds later put the Rockets up 112-99 with 1:30 remaining. Ingram made his debut with the Clippers after sitting out since May following surgery for a heel injury and to repair a partially torn Achilles tendon. The two-time All-Star joined the Clippers in September from Toronto as part of the trade for Kawhi Leonard . He missed the last two games of Toronto’s first-round playoff series against Cleveland because of the injury. He had 16 points and seven rebounds in 27 minutes. Darius Garland had 26 points and eight assists to lead the Clippers, who lost their fourth straight. Rui Hachimura added 19 points. The game was tied midway through the third quarter before the Rockets used a 9-0 run, capped by a 3 from Tari Eason , to make it 74-65. Houston led by 10 entering the fourth. stories.title: Bulls beat Cavaliers 122-108 behind Jordan Hawkins' 19 points and 63 off the bench
stories.summary: — Jordan Hawkins scored a season-high 19 points, Buddy Hield had 17 and the Chicago Bulls got 63 points off the bench as they held on to beat the Cleveland Cavaliers 122-108 on Monday night.
stories.detailText: CHICAGO -- — Jordan Hawkins scored a season-high 19 points, Buddy Hield had 17 and the Chicago Bulls got 63 points off the bench as they held on to beat the Cleveland Cavaliers 122-108 on Monday night. Matas Buzelis added 15 points — all in the first half — as Bulls coach Tiago Splitter spread out playing time after a 151-145 overtime loss to Denver on Sunday. Tre Jones finished with 16 points and nine assists as six Bulls players reached double figures. Chicago shot 45.8% from the field and hit 20 of 49 from 3-point range. Donovan Mitchell led the Cavs with 28 points and James Harden added 21 after the 37-year-old guard scored 51 in their previous game, a 128-119 win over Indiana on Friday. The Bulls put it away with a strong fourth quarter, including a 10-0 spurt capped by Josh Giddey 's finger-roll layup 4:23 in that made it 113-97. Jones hit a quirky 3 with 3:56 to go to make it 120-104. Giddey was limited to four points, 11 assists and two rebounds in 22 minutes after posting 23 points, 14 rebounds and a career-high 22 assists on Sunday. Chicago was clinging to a 93-89 lead entering the fourth quarter after building a 24-point cushion with a big second quarter, when it outscored Cleveland 45-20. The Bulls led 72-50 at halftime. The score was tied 32-all a minute into the second period when the Bulls got hot — buoyed by their bench — while the Cavs went cold. Chicago opened the lead to 24 using a series of runs, including a 12-2 spurt. Chicago shot 49% in the half and hit 11 of 25 from long distance, with Buzelis nailing four 3s. The Cavs responded immediately in the third quarter, starting with a 9-0 run. They outscored Chicago 39-21 in the period to trim it to 93-89 on Mitchell's driving layup with 2 seconds left. Up next Cavaliers: At the New York Knicks on Wednesday. Bulls: At Charlotte on Wednesday. ------ See AP’s full NBA coverage here

stories.title: Lakers 'optimistic' Austin Reaves will play this week
stories.summary: Lakers coach JJ Redick remains "optimistic" about Austin Reaves playing against the San Antonio Spurs on the road Friday.
stories.detailText: Lakers coach JJ Redick remains "optimistic" about Austin Reaves playing against the San Antonio Spurs on the road Friday. Reaves missed his fifth game as the Lakers hosted the Utah Jazz on Monday, Nov. 23. “Today was a big step in terms of getting a stay-ready game in,” Redick told reporters on Monday before the Jazz game. “He played great, moved great, so we are optimistic for the rest of this week.” The Lakers had a successful start to the month with key contributions from the shooting guard. Reaves landed awkwardly on his left heel after missing a transition dunk attempt in the Lakers’ eventual 123-112 victory over the Milwaukee Bucks on Nov. 11. Reaves' return would be welcome, especially against the Spurs, who won the Western Conference last season before falling to the New York Knicks in the NBA Finals. What is Austin Reaves' injury status? Reaves avoided serious injury and was listed as day-to-day by Redick. Reaves and the Lakers' medical staff decided against having imaging done to evaluate the injury further. How Lakers have made up for Austin Reaves' absence Quentin Grimes has taken on more responsibility when the Lakers have been without a star player in the lineup. “I'm not set in stone on anything,” Redick recently told reporters about the possibility of fitting Grimes in as a starter. “The reality is that Quentin has been a starter; either A.R. or Luka has been off, so naturally he will assume some of that usage.” Grimes scored a game-high 47 points on 16-of-24 shooting from the field against the Charlotte Hornets on Nov. 18. Austin Reaves stats Reaves has started all 12 of the games he's played in for the Lakers this season. The guard is averaging 24.7 points, 3.3 rebounds, 4.7 assists and 1.2 steals per game, while shooting 51.3% from the field and 40.9% from beyond the arc. stories.title: Jaden McDaniels scores career-best 34 for Timberwolves in 142-116 rout of Nets
stories.summary: — Jaden McDaniels scored a career-best 34 points and the Minnesota Timberwolves routed the Brooklyn Nets 142-116 on Monday night.
stories.detailText: MINNEAPOLIS -- — Jaden McDaniels scored a career-best 34 points and the Minnesota Timberwolves routed the Brooklyn Nets 142-116 on Monday night. Ayo Dosunmu added 23 as six Timberwolves players reached double figures. Terrence Shannon Jr . had 17 points and five assists off the bench, and Jonathan Kuminga scored 15. McDaniels shot an efficient 12 of 16 from the floor and made all four of his 3-point attempts. He hit a jumper early in the third quarter to reach 30 points for the third time in his regular-season career. The 6-foot-9 forward also had 10 rebounds and six assists. Minnesota set a season high for points, and Brooklyn allowed its most this season. The Timberwolves have won two in a row and four of five. The loss was the fifth straight for the struggling Nets. Julius Randle faced his former team for the first time since the Timberolves traded him to Brooklyn. After two seasons with Minnesota, Randle was dealt in the offseason as part of a four-team swap that helped the Timberwolves land point guard LaMelo Ball from Charlotte. Ball had 17 points in this one. Randle led the Nets with 29 points in his return to Minnesota. He was honored by the Wolves with a pregame video tribute. Mikel Brown Jr . added 17 points for Brooklyn, all in the first half. Brooklyn shot a season-best 50% from 3-point range (18 of 36), but a hot shooting night wasn't enough for a Nets team near the bottom of the Eastern Conference standings. stories.title: Mikel Brown Jr. impresses in first start during Nets night to forget against Timberwolves
stories.summary: Nolan Traore’s hamstring injury is a tough break for the Nets and their second-year pro. But a golden opportunity for rookie Mikel Brown Jr.
stories.detailText: MINNEAPOLIS — Nolan Traore’s hamstring injury is a tough break for the Nets and their second-year pro. But a golden opportunity for rookie Mikel Brown Jr. With Traore sidelined for at least 8-to-10 weeks , Brown finally got his first NBA start Monday at Minnesota. It may not have been a winning one for the lottery pick, but it was an impressive one. The Nets got drubbed 142-116 by the Timberwolves before 18,329 at Target Center. But Brown’s debut in the lineup was one of the few bright spots. Brooklyn Nets guard Mikel Brown Jr. (0) drives past Minnesota Timberwolves center Rudy Gobert (27) during a game in Minneapolis, Monday, Nov. 23, 2026. IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect “Just a normal game. It’s another game for me,” Brown told The Post beforehand. “Whether I come off the bench or whether I start, it’s all about playing hard for four quarters and getting a [win]. So it’s a great opportunity.” Traore was diagnosed with a right hamstring strain, opening the door for Brown, who had heretofore been on a minutes limit and treated with kid gloves. But Monday the training wheels finally came off. Brown finished with 17 points, a career-high seven assists and five rebounds, albeit six turnovers for a Nets team that looked surprisingly fluid but shockingly cavalier and careless. The Nets gave away 21 turnovers for 31 points. Combined with allowing 58 percent shooting and 17-of-39 from deep, they gave themselves no chance to win. They allowed 34 points to Jaden McDaniels and offered no defensive resistance, while Michael Porter Jr. disappeared for long stretches. But Brown was a silver lining. He poured in all of his points in the first half, and finished shooting 4-for-6 from behind the arc, showing deep range and a hair-trigger release. Grant Nelson (16) of the Brooklyn Nets drives to the basket against the Minnesota Timberwolves at Target Center in Minneapolis on Monday, Nov. 23, 2026. NBAE via Getty Images The rookie also combined well with Julius Randle, who had a team-high 29 points in his first clash with the Timberwolves (13-5) since they dealt him to Brooklyn this summer. With Brown at the helm, the Nets shot 52.6 percent and hit 18-for-36 from deep. As much as the Nets will miss Traore — who had leveled up from his rookie season — it was at least an encouraging first start for Brown. Brooklyn Nets guard Mikel Brown Jr. (0) dribbles against Minnesota Timberwolves guard Ayo Dosunmu (13) during a game in Minneapolis, Monday, Nov. 23, 2026. IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect “It’s unfortunate for the kid because he’s had a great summer,” coach Jordi Fernández said of Traore. “He’s about the right things. He’s worked really hard. He’s improved his body, his game. You just saw his confidence out there and his personality and how he communicated [with] his teammates. Everything has been great. Now, it’s not the end of the world. Obviously it’s an injury that we feel for him; he’s already started working and he’ll be back at some point. “Life goes on and we want him around as soon as he can be with the team. And that’s important because his energy was so good, his voice. So, next man mentality. Mikel will have the opportunity to start, and I think that’s also great and it’s exciting. And to [the] question about what his minute restriction is — which I’m not going to tell you — he’ll be able to play starters minutes, whatever that means.” The Nets fell behind 25-12 with 3:54 left in the first on a Jonathan Kuminga layup. They then gave up 10 unanswered to turn a six-point deficit into a 16-point hole. They trailed 74-61 going into the break, and couldn’t rally.

stories.title: Cavs lose 122-108 to Bulls after walloping in first half
stories.summary: The Cavs dug themselves a hole that was too big to climb out of.
stories.detailText: CHICAGO, IL - NOVEMBER 23: James Harden of the Cleveland Cavaliers #1 guards Patrick Williams of the Chicago Bulls #44 during an NBA game on November 23, 2026 at the United Center in Chicago, Illinois. (Photo by Melissa Tamez/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The Cleveland Cavaliers lost 122-108 to the Chicago Bulls after taking a beating in the first half. Donovan Mitchell led the team with 28 points. The second quarter was an outright disaster. Chicago opened up with a 19-6 run in the first four minutes, and would extend that to 32-10 on their way to a dominant lead. Cleveland entered tonight as the 10th-worst transition defense in the league. It showed. The Bulls broke free in transition over and over again in the second quarter. The Cavs couldn’t keep up or slow them down, and Chicago reaped the rewards. Everything from poor effort to bad communication contributed to this. But more than anything, the Cavs couldn’t score the ball to regain control of the pace. Missed shots and turnovers led to more fast-break opportunities for the opponent. That wasn’t all. Chicago’s bench opened the game by outscoring Cleveland 48-9 in the first half. The first quarter was mostly fine, but the second quarter was a running rampage from the Bulls. The Cavs trailed by 22 points going into halftime. It was an inspiring start to the third quarter that gave the Cavs life. They jumped out to a quick start, chipping away at the Bulls by working downhill into the paint and playing with an advantage. Converting those opportunities helped them regain control of the game’s pace. James Harden was instrumental in the Cavs’ run. He probed into the paint and either scored, dished an assist, or drew a foul throughout the third quarter. Harden scored 11 of his 21 points in the third quarter. Cleveland would eventually get the game to within two possessions, but fell back down by double digits once the Bulls reignited their flame in the fourth quarter. It was a strong second half from the Cavs, but they gave themselves too thin a margin of error to complete the comeback. That’s what happens when you lose the second quarter by 25 points. Not to mention, the Bulls took 17 more shot attempts than Cleveland. Jordan Hawkins lit it up for 19 points off the bench on 7-for-13 shooting. It was a confident performance from a younger player who is trying to establish himself in the NBA. The Cavs certainly won’t forget him the next time they play Hawkins. Cleveland falls to 9-9 on the season and will play the New York Knicks on Wednesday.

stories.title: Siakam scores 20 and comes up big late as Pacers snap 4-game skid with 125-120 win over Thunder
stories.summary: — Pascal Siakam scored 20 points, including a 3-pointer with 44.4 seconds to go, and Kelly Oubre Jr. added a season-high 20 points to help the Indiana Pacers snap a four-game losing streak with a 125-120 victory over the Oklahoma City Thunder on...
stories.detailText: INDIANAPOLIS -- — Pascal Siakam scored 20 points, including a 3-pointer with 44.4 seconds to go, and Kelly Oubre Jr . added a season-high 20 points to help the Indiana Pacers snap a four-game losing streak with a 125-120 victory over the Oklahoma City Thunder on Monday night. The Pacers finished 15 of 37 on 3-pointers and looked much more like the team that made the 2025 NBA Finals by pushing the tempo, knocking down long-range shots and spreading the scoring. Six players scored in double figures, including Jalen Slawson with 16, Andrew Nembhard with 15 and Ivica Zubac who had 14 points and 15 rebounds. Obi Toppin finished with 17 points and six rebounds. Two-time league MVP Shai Gilgeous-Alexander kept short-handed Oklahoma City close with 38 points. Kenrich Williams made four 3s and finished with 20 points, and Isaiah Hartenstein finished with 18 points and nine rebounds. But it wasn't quite enough to prevent the Thunder from suffering a second straight loss. What was supposed to be the first matchup between Tyrese Haliburton and the Thunder since Game 7 of the 2025 NBA Finals never materialized. Haliburton missed his 14th straight game with a strained left hamstring and only four of Monday's starters also started that Game 7 — Gilgeous-Alexander and Hartenstein of the Thunder and Nembhard and Siakam for the Pacers. Indiana never trailed after going on a 9-0 run to take a 27-19 lead late in the first quarter. The Pacers still led 56-51 and extended the margin to 70-58 in the third quarter before a back-and-forth final quarter. The Thunder cut the deficit to one twice in the final 1:31, but Siakam answered each time with a jumper, the second a 3 to give Indiana a 123-119 with 44.4 seconds left, and Oubre's late block of a layup preserved the lead. Up next Thunder: Return home to face Minnesota on Wednesday. stories.summary: It felt like one of those nights.
stories.detailText: PHILADELPHIA, PA - NOVEMBER 23: LeBron James #23 of the Philadelphia 76ers dribbles the ball during the game against the Portland Trail Blazers on November 23, 2026 at Xfinity Mobile Arena in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania NOTE TO USER: User expressly acknowledges and agrees that, by downloading and/or using this Photograph, user is consenting to the terms and conditions of the Getty Images License Agreement. Mandatory Copyright Notice: Copyright 2026 NBAE (Photo by Jesse D. Garrabrant/NBAE via Getty Images) | NBAE via Getty Images We haven’t seen them yet this year — do all Western Conference teams just never miss their three-pointers? The Sixers were blown out by the Trail Blazers 128-111 Monday as Portland made 45% of their threes on the night. After missing his last two games, Jaylen Brown was soaring until he ran into foul trouble, finishing with 20 points on 8-of-14 shooting along with two rebounds and four assists. LeBron James had his best shooting night as a Sixer, going 8-of-13 from the floor to finish with a season-high 23 points along with seven rebounds and three assists. Tyrese Maxey had 22 points and five assists on 7-of-16 shooting. VJ Edgecombe finished with 12 points, seven rebounds and seven assists shooting 5-of-11 from the field. Deni Avdija led all scorers with 31. Joel Embiid (illness) was the only Sixer out tonight. Ja Morant and Shaedon Sharp were out for Portland, both out with long-term injuries. Here are some thoughts at the buzzer. First Quarter The Sixers got Brown involved with two early touches. He drew a foul on the first and got an open jumper on the second thanks to a healthy stiff arm to Avdija. Jabari Walker found Edgecombe by the basket as the Blazers were trying to get down the floor, capping off a 9-2 Philly run to start the game and prompt an early timeout for the Blazers. That timeout got Avdija going offensively. After beating Brown off the dribble he nailed a couple of threes. LeBron was creating threes on the other end as well. A pumpfake of his sent Avdija flying by, allowing James to drill an open one from the corner. He drove baseline on the next possession and found Brown, also wide open in the corner. Coming off the bench, Dominick Barlow was the first able to stop Avdija, swatting away a layup attempt. The Sixers didn’t come out with a poor effort defensively. They were able to lock up Damian Lillard for a sho-tclock violation, but Portland opened the game hot from deep, making four of their first nine threes of the game. Dominick Barlow with the block, LeBron James with the jam pic.twitter.com/lKxfObel9a — Liberty Ballers (@Liberty_Ballers) November 24, 2026 Adem Bona also returned after missing time with a neck injury. He was able to quickly grab an offensive rebound upon entering the game and when the ball got swung to him, he was able to put it on the deck and get to the basket for a dunk. He even hit a bit of a move to get by Jrue Holiday. He was relieved by Walker after only a couple of minutes. Walker picked up a missed Dean Wade three and put it back to keep the Sixers up by two after the first. Second Quarter With some more starters back on the floor the offense started to hum again. Brown and Edgecombe each drilled pull-up jumpers. LeBron threw a pair of nice passes to Walker who converted on both of them, and got a skyhook for himsel. Defensively, Walker was a pretty small look against Donovan Clingan. The Sixers tried to sit in some zone to combat that, but quickly went back to man. On top of those paint concerns, the Blazers remained pretty hot from three. They hit two more to take a lead of their own, despite LeBron hitting a big three that got the crowd off it’s feet in between them. Brown did not look like he had missed the last two games at all. He just looked so smooth getting to his spots in the midrange. He put up 19 in the first half on 10 shots. The Sixers needed every bit of it because they had less answers for Avdija on the other end. After starting the game with Brown on Avdija, the Sixers tried Dean Wade before ultimately landing on Barlow to close the half. Barlow did foul him but Avdija missed both free throws. On the next trip down Barlow was able to force a bad airball that happened to fall to LeBron who threw a gorgeous fullcourt pass to Brown for the fast break dunk. After that tied the game, Lillard was able to draw a foul on Edgecombe shooting a three-pointer. Maxey found LeBron in the corner on the ensuing possession for another Sixers’ buzzer-beater, keeping the game tied at the half. Ridiculous LeBron James Pass of the Game so far… an absolute dime pic.twitter.com/UPXMCYfYfr — Erin Grugan (@eringrugan) November 24, 2026 THE KING. 👑 pic.twitter.com/m1JobqUsuQ — Liberty Ballers (@Liberty_Ballers) November 24, 2026 Third Quarter LeBron tried to throw another fullcourt bounce pass to give Maxey a fast break layup, but Sidy Cissoko got his hands on it to break it up. They continued to move the ball well though as Edgecombe got open in the dunker for James to find him, before dishing to a cutting Walker who drew a foul. Both teams struggled from the line to start the second half as Walker split his pair. Avdija was unable to convert an and-1 and Clingan gave the fans a five-count of chicken nuggets very early. The Sixers also had to deal with another extended period of Brown on the bench after he picked up his fourth foul. James seemed to still be up to carry the scoring load, drilling his fourth three of the night on his fourth attempt. . @KingJames a perfect 4-4 from three! pic.twitter.com/LLLNdcV69g — Philadelphia 76ers (@sixers) November 24, 2026 For as good as LeBron was, the Sixers struggled to supplement him offensively with Brown sitting in foul trouble. They had a six-minute stretch only scoring one field goal. Maxey tried to get more aggressive but had a pull-up three attempt blocked by Robert Williams III. Lucky for him the Blazers weren’t able to secure the rebound and Maxey was able to scoot to the basket for a reverse layup. Any minor blip for the Sixers offense was notable because they just could not get stops on the other end. As they sat in a zone Portland continued to drill everything from deep. After Scoot Henderson drifted into a gap to drill a three, Holiday hit one in Wade’s face on the following possession. On the other end Barlow was desperately trying to create a hustle bucket, but he came up a bit gingerly after going for a rebound and getting his shot blocked by Cissoko. Jayson Kent drilled one from the corner to give the Blazers a nine-point lead as the third came to a close. Fourth Quarter Henderson and Kent drilled a couple more threes to start the quarter, extending Portland’s lead to its largest of the night. Nick Nurse tried to let it ride as LeBron got to the basket, but after Edgecombe dribbled the ball off his foot out of bounds and the team surrendered a layup off an offensive rebound, Nurse called an angry timeout less than two minutes into the quarter. Edgecombe was able to run out off a loose ball and get a transition layup and the Blazers immediately called a timeout to squash a potential run. The Sixers had chances coming out of the timeout, forcing a couple turnovers, but they couldn’t take advantage on the offensive end. Lillard hit a pull-up which got the Blazers offense rolling again and the Sixers had no response. Portland’s height advantage had begun to wear the Sixers down as well as they started surrendering more. offensive rebounds. No matter what center option the Sixers tried, Portland’s center would have an inch or two in height advantage, there was just nothing to be done about that, save for some Tacko time. Avdija stole an inbounds pass of off Maxey as Sixers fans started to flock to the exits with over five minutes remaining.

stories.detailText: Austin Reaves’ left heel injury sidelined him for the fifth consecutive game on Monday . But he also took an important step in his return-to-play process before the Lakers hosted the Jazz again at Crypto.com Arena, leaving the team optimistic about his availability to return later in the week. Austin Reaves has been sidelined for five games because of his heel injury. NBAE via Getty Images Reaves participated in a “stay-ready” game on Monday after the team’s shootaround at their practice facility as he recovers from his bruised left heel. The star guard was a full participant in Sunday’s practice , but it didn’t include any live action. The Lakers ruled him out for Monday’s game Sunday evening after coach JJ Redick said Reaves was “making progress.” Austin Reaves (15) of the Los Angeles Lakers shoots a free throw. stories.title: Victor Wembanyama missing first game of season due to back tightness, De'Aaron Fox also out vs. Kings
stories.summary: Both Spurs stars are expected to return for Wednesday's NBA Cup game against the Portland Trail Blazers.
stories.detailText: The San Antonio Spurs were without both Victor Wembanyama and De'Aaron Fox on Monday night. Wembanyama was ruled out of the Spurs' game against the Sacramento Kings due to back tightness, the team announced shortly before the game was set to tip off at the Golden 1 Center. Fox is dealing with a shin contusion, and was ruled out at the same time. While losing two star players for any contest is undoubtedly concerning, the two injuries were described as simply "bumps and bruises" by San Antonio Express-News' Jeff McDonald . Spurs coach Mitch Johnson said both players are not expected to be sidelined long, but would not yet declare they would be ready to return for their NBA Cup matchup against the Portland Trail Blazers on Wednesday. The game against the Kings is the first that Wembanyama has missed all season. He's averaged 29.9 points, 12.3 rebounds and 3.9 blocks through the first 17 games of the season, all of which are career highs for the 22-year-old. He's fresh off a wild 50-point outing on Saturday night . Wembanyama outscored the New Orleans Pelicans starters by himself in the first half before rolling to a dominant win. It was his second 50-point game already this season, following a 52-point performance against the Dallas Mavericks earlier this fall. Fox has averaged 12.4 points and 5.8 assists per game this season. The 28-year-old is in his second full season with the Spurs, who landed him in a deal with the Kings during the 2024-25 campaign. Johnson said Fox was injured when he was intentionally tripped by a Pelicans player. The Spurs were 14-3 entering Monday's contest in Sacramento, which is tied for the best record in the league. The Kings, meanwhile, are just 2-14 and have won only one of their 10 home games so far this season.

stories.title: Lakers rookie discovers surprising NBA perks he never dreamed of
stories.summary: Consider Lakers rookie Cameron Carr among the players learning about the lesser-known benefits of his profession.
stories.detailText: There are several commonly known perks of being an NBA player. Chartered flights. State-of-the-art facilities. And a lot of free, high-quality food are among them. Cameron Carr #43 of the Los Angeles Lakers smiles during a game against the Utah Jazz. NBAE via Getty Images But there are several that aren’t as well known that an athlete doesn’t become aware of until they’re in the NBA. Consider Cameron Carr among the players learning about the benefits of his profession. The Lakers rookie wing was posed with the question of unexpected benefits of being an NBA player that he didn’t anticipate after Monday’s shootaround ahead of his team’s home game against the Jazz at Crypto.com Arena. Cameron Carr of the Los Angeles Lakers drives to the basket for a layup. NBAE via Getty Images His answers didn’t disappoint. “I’ll probably say NBA League Pass,” Carr responded. “Got NBA League Pass for free. Never had NBA League Pass.” The former Baylor Bear couldn’t contain his excitement over getting the NBA’s product for free that can cost $159.99/year or $24.99/month. Now, he can watch any NBA game at any time. “So s— great,” Carr said before covering his mouth in a slight panic for cursing. “It’s great, by the way.” Cameron Carr of the Los Angeles Lakers speaks to the media after a game. NBAE via Getty Images Sandro Mamukelashvili , a six-year veteran, understood Carr’s excitement. “Yeah, it’s amazing,” Mamukelashvili said. “Watch every game [for] free. Give it to your parents. I definitely enjoy my free league pass.” The second perk appealed to Carr’s appreciation of pregame naps. “They do like the Sleep Number stuff for the rookies,” he said. “They do like a discount code, so that’s great.” He added: “I’m a big sleep guy. Like as soon as I get done with this, I’m gonna shower, go home, and take a nap.”

stories.title: Warriors star clowns on Jayson Tatum with ‘Friday’ spoof after he miss at the buzzer
stories.summary: Jayson Tatum missed a chance to beat the Warriors at the buzzer. Jimmy Butler had just the meme for the occasion. After Golden State edged Boston 88-87 on Sunday night...
stories.detailText: Jayson Tatum missed a chance to beat the Warriors at the buzzer. Jimmy Butler had just the meme for the occasion. After Golden State edged Boston 88-87 on Sunday night to snap a five-game losing streak, Butler shared an AI spoof casting his old playoff rival as Red, the guy who gets his chain snatched in “Friday.” Boston Celtics guard Jayson Tatum, right, looks to shoot against Golden State Warriors center Charles Bassey (28) and guard De’Anthony Melton (8) on Nov. 22, 2026. AP Photo/Jeff Chiu In the scene behind the meme , neighborhood bully Deebo takes the chain Red’s grandmother gave him while his buddies Craig and Smokey look on. Once Deebo leaves, Red wants to know why neither of them helped. When he finally makes a run for his car, his friends have a pretty good idea where he’s headed. “He’s gonna cry in the car.” An AI-generated “Friday” spoof depicts Jayson Tatum patting Draymond Green on the shoulder as Brandin Podziemski sits beside him. (Screengrab via Jimmy Butler/Instagram) Jimmy Butler on IG pic.twitter.com/d0JM9bFmIr — aly ✶ (@jinthirty) November 23, 2026 In the spoof Butler shared , Draymond Green and Brandin Podziemski take Craig and Smokey’s spots on the porch. Tatum, in his green No. 0 Celtics jersey, pats Green on the shoulder before taking off for the hatchback with Red’s funny little run. The camera cuts back to Green, mouth hanging open. Tatum had a few reasons to want that final minute in San Francisco back. He missed a free throw that would have tied the game with 56 seconds left, then missed a go-ahead 3-pointer with 30 seconds to play. Hugo González gave Boston one more chance by stripping Green, but Tatum’s contested 16-footer missed at the horn. Jimmy Butler III #10 and Stephen Curry #30 smile during a game against the New Orleans Pelicans at Chase Center in San Francisco on Monday, Nov. 9, 2026. NBAE via Getty Images Tatum finished with 27 points, 10 rebounds and six assists as Boston dropped its fourth straight. Podziemski led Golden State with 18 points and seven rebounds. Butler and Tatum met in three Eastern Conference finals in four years during Butler’s time in Miami. Back then, getting the last word on Tatum could take Butler seven games. On Sunday, all it took was an Instagram post.

stories.title: Cameron Boozer injury update: Grizzlies share status of Rookie of the Year contender
stories.summary: The Memphis Grizzlies said star rookie Cameron Boozer suffered a sprained ankle and gave a timetable for when he will be reevaluated.
stories.detailText: The Memphis Grizzlies have an injury update on their star rookie. On Monday, Nov. 23, the Grizzlies released a statement saying that Cameron Boozer suffered a sprained right ankle in the third quarter of their game against the Golden State Warriors . The Grizzlies went on to win 126-98 on Thursday, Nov. 19. The 19-year-old "underwent imaging that revealed a moderate-grade medial sprain," the team said. Boozer is out at least four weeks, when he will be reevaluated. Memphis said he is expected to make a full recovery. He already missed the Grizzlies' 104-95 loss to the Minnesota Timberwolves on Saturday, Nov. 21. Last week, USA TODAY Sports ranked Boozer as the top rookie of the season so far , beating out top pick AJ Dybantsa of the Washington Wizards and rookie sensation Yaxel Lendeborg of the Warriors. Boozer was selected out of Duke by the Grizzlies as the No. 3 overall pick in this spring's NBA draft. He was behind Dybantsa and the second pick, Darryn Peterson, who was taken by the Utah Jazz . Memphis is fifth in the Western Conference with a record of 12-5. Cameron Boozer stats Boozer is averaging 16.6 points with 9.2 rebounds and 5.3 assists per game in his rookie year. He is the Grizzlies' second-leading scorer behind Ty Jerome, who is averaging 24.8 points per outing. In a 136-120 win against the Wizards last week, Boozer had his best scoring night yet with 29 points. He added seven boards and seven assists and went 7-of-13 from behind the arc. The former Blue Devils standout has notched four double-doubles so far this season. He had a triple-double with 18 points, 12 rebounds and 12 assists in a 124-103 win over the Portland Trail Blazers last month. stories.title: One of Walker Kessler’s greatest skills? Helping the Lakers build chemistry
stories.summary: No one thought the Lakers would gel this quickly. Not with nine new players. But in the Lakers’ locker room, one of those new guys has expedited the process by...
stories.detailText: No one thought the Lakers would gel this quickly. Not with nine new players. But in the Lakers’ locker room, one of those new guys has expedited the process by being a generator of good vibes. Walker Kessler is a beast on the court who’s known as one of the best rebounders and rim protectors in the league . Walker Kessler of the Utah Jazz walks out during a game against the Los Angeles Lakers in Los Angeles, Wednesday, Nov. 18, 2026. NBAE via Getty Images But off the court, he has done something equally if not more important: he has made it so that the Lakers look forward to coming to work every day. “We all love Walk,” Ziaire Williams said. “He’s the anchor of our defense. You know, he’s one of the nicest guys I think I’ve probably ever played with. He’s a great dude, man. Love Walk to death. It’s always good to know, you know, you have this paint presence behind you, top 1% of the 1% in rim protection. So, yeah, he’s been great for us.” Kessler is averaging 14.3 points, 10.7 rebounds and 2.1 blocks per game for the Lakers, who are tied for the best record in the league (14-3) with the Spurs and 76ers and are considered title contenders . But his impact extends beyond the box score. He takes responsibility, such as when Lakers coach JJ Redick lit into him after he had only six points and one rebound at halftime against the Kings on Friday. He went on to finish with 15 points, seven rebounds and three blocked shots. Dylan Cardwell #32 of the Sacramento Kings plays defense on Walker Kessler #14 of the Los Angeles Lakers in Los Angeles, California, Friday, Nov. 20, 2026. NBAE via Getty Images “I wasn’t playing physical,” Kessler said after the Lakers’ 106-104 win. “I wasn’t going up to dunk the ball. I was missing some more touches around the rim. And then defensively, being undisciplined. Jumping at stuff I don’t need to jump at. He definitely lit into me. It was good. I needed it. That’s what makes a good coach. Knowing when guys need that and when guys don’t.” Kessler encourages those around him, such as letting the perimeter defenders know they can take risks and aggressively go for steals because he has their back if a player blows past them. It has led to the Lakers leading the league in steals with 10.6 per game. “Walker absorbs my mistakes,” Matisse Thybulle said. When Kessler was told his words, he balked. “I promise you he’s absorbing my mistakes, too,” Kessler said. “There are times when I’ll overcommit on a float or something and he’ll back down on the big or get a steal in the passing lane or play the pocket or swipe down. So it goes both ways.” Walker Kessler of the Los Angeles Lakers shoots a 3-point basket against the Sacramento Kings on Friday, Nov. 20, 2026, at Crypto.com Arena in Los Angeles. NBAE via Getty Images There’s just a symbiosis between the Lakers’ defensive leader and everyone else. He wants to do well for them. And the feeling is reciprocated. He enters rooms smiling. He always thanks reporters. It’s funny because Kessler began generating that type of good will as soon as the Lakers acquired him from the Jazz in July in a sign-and-trade for two first-round picks and two first-round pick swaps on top of a four-year, $180 million deal. When Kessler was asked about the Lakers emptying their treasure trove of draft assets to acquire him, he didn’t hold back. “I’m somebody that if I know that they have that belief in me, I’m gonna run through a brick wall for them,” Kessler said. “That’s just how I’ve been wired my whole life.” Kessler is still finding his rhythm after playing only five games for the Jazz last season before suffering a torn labrum in his left shoulder that required surgery. After finishing with fewer than 10 rebounds in his first five games, Redick challenged him to be more aggressive on the boards, including rebounding outside his space. The big man responded by having double-doubles in nine of his next 11 games. Walker Kessler #14 of the Los Angeles Lakers and Matisse Thybulle #4 play in the fourth quarter on Friday, Nov. 20, 2026, at Crypto.com Arena in Los Angeles. Getty Images “It’s not an easy thing to come back and be thrown in that fire, especially to do the things that he’s doing,” Collin Sexton said. “It’s amazing, you know, to see. So we all have to make sure that we’re uplifting him because it’s not easy to just be out eight, nine months and just go back out there and do what he’s doing. So I always tell him like he’s doing a hell of a job.” Still, there’s a feeling that Kessler hasn’t even reached his potential yet, even though he’s every bit of the franchise center the Lakers hoped to acquire. But through Kessler’s ups and downs on the court, one thing has remained consistent. His good attitude. Kessler wants this to work. He wants the Lakers to be great. And it’s obvious that he’s inspiring everyone around him to deeply share that desire by how he carries himself and encourages those around him. “Yeah, I mean, yeah, it’s often overlooked, you know?” Williams said. “There are guys in the league who don’t have the best interest [of others] and people skills and are just [in] their mind. Just focused on just whatever they got to do, you know? But Walk, he’s a team-first player and just makes the vibes and the locker room and just the flow of the game just so much easier.”

stories.title: The 76ers are fun again, so it's the return of Roob's 76ers Stats!
stories.summary: Some pretty astounding stats as the East-leading Sixers are 13-3 on the season.
stories.detailText: The 76ers are fun again, so it's the return of Roob's 76ers Stats! originally appeared on NBC Sports Philadelphia This 76ers team is a heck of a lot of fun to watch and fun basketball means fun stats! At 13-3, the 76ers are exactly a month into the 5 th -best start in franchise history and best since they were 14-2 in 2000-01. Which turned out to be a pretty good year. They were 15-1 in 1949-50 and 1966-67 and 14-2 in 1981-82. To help everybody get through this interminable two-day gap between 76ers games, here’s our first 2026-27 installment of Roob’s 76ers Stats, with a tip of the hat to Stathead. → The 76ers have been out-rebounded by 34 through 16 games (719-685) and their 13-3 record matches the best in NBA history by a team that’s been out-rebounded after 16 games. Three other teams have been 13-3 despite getting out-rebounded, most recently the 2013-14 Miami Heat. The others are the 1979-80 Bucks and 2012-2013 Spurs. The 76ers are an NBA-best 6-3 this year when they’ve been out-rebounded (which means they’re 7-0 when they have a rebounding edge). → In the win over Orlando Thursday, V.J. Edgecombe had 24 points, eight rebounds, six assists and two steals, and Joel Embiid had 26 points, six rebounds, seven assists and two steals. It was the first time two 76ers had at least 24 points, six rebounds and assists and two steals in a game in 53 years. In a win over the Celtics at the Spectrum in 1973, Fred Carter had 31 points, six rebounds, six assists and seven steals and George McGinniss had 28 points, 16 rebounds, eight assists and three steals. → Kentavious Caldwell-Pope, a career 37 percent shooter from 3, is shooting 44 percent so far. Anfernee Simons, a career 38 percent shooter from 3, is shooting 41 percent. Jabari Walker, a career 33 percent 3-point shooter, is at 42 percent. Dean Wade, a career 37 percent shooter, is at 41 percent. Jaylen Brown, a career 36 percent shooter from range, is at 39 percent. The 76ers are shooting just 36 percent as a team from the stripe because James and Embiid have been so bad, but everybody else is off to career-best starts from 3-point range. → The 76ers are 7-1 on the road, equalling their best road record ever after eight games. They were also 7-1 in 1980-81, 1981-82 and 1982-83. The 1981 team had the best road start in franchise history, going 12-1 before losing its second road game. → With 15.7 points, 6.8 assists and 6.8 rebounds per game, LeBron James is only the fifth 76er ever to average at least 15 ½ points and 6 ½ assists and rebounds through 16 games. The others are some familiar names: Wilt Chamberlain in 1967, Charles Barkley in 1987, Ben Simmons in 2018 and James Harden in 2023. → The 76ers already have more wins this year after trailing by 10 points through the first quarter than all but two full seasons since 1950. They had four in 1985-86 and again in 2022-23. The Hawks also have three wins this year when trailing by double digits after the first quarter, but they’re 3-4 and the 76ers are 3-2. So they actually have a winning record when they’re down by double digits going into the second quarter. → With Jaylen Brown (22.6, 6.6), Joel Embiid (20.0, 8.3), LeBron James (15.7, 6.8) and V.J. Edgecombe (13.6, 6.5), the 76ers are the only NBA team with four players averaging 6 ½ rebounds and 13 points. The last time they had four players in a season who averaged 13 points and 6 ½ rebounds was 1961-62 when they were the Syracuse Nationals, with Dave Gambee (16.7, 7.9), Hal Greer (22.8, 7.4), Red Kerr (16.3, 14.7), Dolph Schayes (14.7, 7.8) and Lee Shaffer (16.9, 6.8). → Edgecombe’s 6.5 rebounds per game are 2 nd -most among shooting guards behind only the Grizzlies’ Cedric Coward, who is at 8.5. Edgecombe’s 6.5 is also 2 nd -highest ever by a 76ers shooting guard behind only Greer’s 7.4 during that 1961-62 season. Edgecombe averaged 5.6 rebounds as a rookie and his 5.8 career average is highest by a shooting guard who spent more than one year with the 76ers. Greer is second at 5.3. Among all NBA players who’ve played at least 90 games, Edgecombe’s 5.8 average is 11 th -highest all-time among shooting guards (although Stathead includes some swing guard-forwards in their data). → Joel Embiid’s 14.6 shooting percentage from 3 is worst in NBA history after 16 games (minimum 40 attempts). Embiid is 6-for-41 from the stripe this year. The previous 3-point shooting low 16 games into a season belonged to Cedric Ceballos of the Lakers in 1995-96 and the 76ers’ Evan Turner in 2013-14. Both were 6-for-43 for 16.3 percent. → LeBron James is at 22.2 percent from 3 on 10-for-45. The Sixers are the first NBA team in 12 years with two players under 23 percent after 16 games with a minimum of 40 attempts. In 2014 Tony Wroten was 10-for-50 (10 percent) and Turner was 6-for-43 (16.3 percent).

stories.detailText: Embiid sidelined for Sixers-Blazers with illness originally appeared on NBC Sports Philadelphia The Sixers ruled star center Joel Embiid out with an illness Monday night for their game against the Trail Blazers at Xfinity Mobile Arena. Embiid first popped up on the Sixers’ injury report at 11:45 a.m. ET when the team listed him as questionable. He was downgraded to out about 90 minutes before the 7 p.m. tip-off. The 32-year-old big man played in the 14 of the Eastern Conference-leading Sixers ’ first 17 games and averaged 20.4 points, 8.9 rebounds and 4.1 assists. He was the team’s top scorer in each of the last three games and finished one assist shy of a 26-point triple-double Saturday in the Sixers’ win over the Bucks. The Sixers entered Monday 2-1 this season in games without Embiid. They were 21-23 last year. Outside of Embiid, the Sixers are in good shape health-wise. Jalen Brown, Dean Wade and Adem Bona are all set to return from injuries against Portland. Ariel Hukporti (right Achilles tendon tear) is out indefinitely. The Sixers went with a starting five of Tyrese Maxey, VJ Edgecombe, Brown, LeBron James and Jabari Walker. stories.title: James sees a lot to like — and improve — for East-leading Sixers
stories.summary: The Sixers sit at 14-3 and lead the Eastern Conference after beating the Bucks.
stories.detailText: James sees a lot to like — and improve — for East-leading Sixers originally appeared on NBC Sports Philadelphia LeBron James likes to refer to the NBA season as a “marathon.” A few miles in, the Sixers lead the Eastern Conference pack. With 17 regular-season contests down of 82, the team sits at 14-3, which is 2.5 games ahead of the second-seeded Celtics. The Sixers squeaked out their latest win, a 132-129 decision Saturday over the cellar-dwelling Bucks , but the bottom line is they’ve become accustomed to finding many routes to victory. “We want to build habits,” James said. “We want to try to take steps forward every game that we get the opportunity. I know sometimes it doesn’t happen that way, but we want to do it. “We want to strive to be as great as we can offensively, defensively and on special teams. A win is a win, but there’s ways to win and ways to try to continue to build habits over the course of a marathon.” All sorts of Sixers games have gone down to the wire and they’ve won every single one. The team is an incredible 12-0 in clutch situations , defined as games with a point differential of five or under in the final five minutes. The Sixers rank third in the NBA in clutch offensive rating (140.3) and third in clutch net rating (plus-42.0). “It’s good to build that part of our game,” James said. “Obviously, we wanted to close the game out a lot better. But a team like that, we know they’re going to be scrappy. They’re going to play as hard as they can for 48 minutes. … We can learn from that.” James was the centerpiece of the Sixers’ fourth-quarter offense Saturday. He scored 13 of his 21 points between the 7:46 and 3:13 mark of the fourth. The four-time MVP got two buckets on no-nonsense drives and another on an after-timeout isolation hoop over rookie Brayden Burries. James also scored three times on a designed Horns action where he brought the ball up, used Tyrese Maxey’s back screen at the elbow and caused serious problems for Milwaukee in the paint. “We continue to add things to the half-court offense and also to the late-game package,” Sixers head coach Nick Nurse said. “That’s something we added a few game ago. It’s one of those things where, especially if we’re in the bonus, we’ve got some big bodies that can cut down the lane and have feel for timing. It was working. Just keep going to it.” James has grown in comfort with Nurse’s coaching style. He knows the Sixers expect him to be a de facto coach on the floor, too. “I’m just trying to be there for the team in any capacity they want,” he said. “Just trying to be an extension of his calls and his commands out there on the floor. Trying to make his life and his job a little bit easier as well. “But it’s been great, not only with him but the whole coaching staff. They’ve welcomed me with open arms and allowed me to kind of be the voice for the team every day, and take that responsibility.” After a tremendous first impression defensively and some subpar offensive nights, the Sixers’ numbers have recently evened out. The team is 12th in offensive rating outside of garbage time and 12th in defensive rating, per Cleaning the Glass. In essence, the Sixers have been a bit above average on both ends of the floor and downright brilliant in the closing minutes. It’s all added up to an early lead in a very long race. “I think we’ve bought into the pass,” James said. “We have so many guys that can score the ball at elite levels. … In order for us to be a super-complete team, I think the power of the pass is very infectious. And it’s also key for our other guys, to make sure they feel in a rhythm and they feel confident. We’ve done that from Day 1 and I think it’s gotten better and better. … And I think our defense has been really good for the majority of the season. “(Today) it wasn’t so great, but we’ve been very good defensively throughout the course of the season. … I don’t want to say there’s anything bad. There’s so many things for us to do better for sure. There’s games where we can defensive rebound a lot better and there’s games where we can not turn the ball over (as much). And there’s games where we can be a little more phsyical defensively at the point of attack like (today). “I wouldn’t say anything has been bad, though. That’s a good thing. We want to continue to have room for improvement and we don’t want to be great in November. That would be weird.”

teamStories.detailText: SACRAMENTO, Calif. -- Ninety minutes prior to tipoff Monday, the San Antonio Spurs ruled Victor Wembanyama and De'Aaron Fox out of their game against the Sacramento Kings . The Spurs are anticipating both will return for the team's Wednesday night game against the Portland Trail Blazers in advance of a showcase Friday night NBA Cup game at home against the 14-3 Los Angeles Lakers . Wembanyama is sitting with lower back tightness after appearing in each of the team's first 17 games. Fox is out with a right shin contusion after he was kicked during a recent win over the New Orleans Pelicans . The Spurs are already without Dylan Harper , who is expected to miss between one and three weeks with a hip strain. In the absence of three of their biggest names, the 14-3 Spurs are starting Stephon Castle , Devin Vassell , Julian Champagnie , Harrison Barnes and Luke Kornet against the 2-14 Kings. The Boston Celtics did something similar Saturday night, resting Jayson Tatum and Derrick White on the front side of a back-to-back in Sacramento. They were ultimately burned, losing 97-96 to a Kings team that entered the night winless at home. The Spurs have already blown the Kings out twice this season. Wembanyama had 29 points, 10 rebounds and five blocks in the first win in San Antonio and another 30 points and 14 rebounds in an easy win in Sacramento two weeks ago. Wembanyama is averaging a jaw-dropping 29.9 points, 12.3 rebounds and 3.9 blocks through 17 games, compiling 33 more blocks and 38 more dunks than the next-closest NBA player.

stories.title: Commanders' Jayden Daniels-themed post aimed at Bengals tops NFL Week 11 trolls
stories.summary: NFL teams remained petty in Week 11, led by a post from the Washington Commanders.
stories.detailText: The unlikeliest of victories can often feel the sweetest -- especially when it can be capped with a troll. The Washington Commanders beat the Cincinnati Bengals 22-20 on "Monday Night Football." Washington faced a one-point deficit with 46 seconds left after Cincinnati kicked a go-ahead field goal. The Commanders, though, had the last laugh. Quarterback Jayden Daniels connected with wide receiver Antonio Williams twice during the final drive, including a 42-yard reception that set up a field goal. Drew Stevens nailed the 26-yarder as time expired, ensuring Washington's victory. The Commanders poked fun at the Bengals on social media in clever fashion. They posted a clip from a 2001 episode of the talk show "Maury," during which someone on the show shares their phobia of aluminum foil. While on stage, someone walks toward them with aluminum foil, prompting them to run off stage and yell, "Get away from me." Washington put its spin on the video, editing the host Maury Povich as "Monday Night Football," the lady with the aluminum foil fear as the Bengals and the aluminum foil as Daniels, who is 2-0 against the Bengals on "Monday Night Football." Here are the top trolls from the NFL's Week 11. Buffalo Bills 26, Miami Dolphins 9 Grand Theft Auto VI has taken over the entertainment world since its release Thursday. The video game's reach also carried over to the NFL, becoming the theme of a petty post Sunday. The Buffalo Bills defeated the Miami Dolphins led by its defense. Buffalo gave up only 185 yards and picked off Dolphins quarterback Kyle McCord once. Josh Allen had two interceptions himself, but he also threw for 304 yards and a score. Other teams such as the New York Jets and Chicago Bears tapped into the GTA VI space, but the Bills' attempt felt more direct as they faced the Dolphins. The victory prompted Buffalo to post a custom game cover inspired by that of GTA VI, which is set in "Vice City," a fictional version of Miami. Instead of it reading "GTA VI" across the cover, the Bills added: "Bills Win" with players scattered throughout it. Carolina Panthers 35, Baltimore Ravens 33 It required a late stop, but the Carolina Panthers pulled out a wild victory against the Baltimore Ravens . Carolina went ahead on a 37-yard field goal with 1:44 left. Baltimore received possession with a chance to go ahead before Jacoby Brissett was picked off with 36 seconds left, clinching the Panthers' win. A clever caption kicked off Carolina's trolling as it wrote: "Came down to the wire," with "the wire" being a reference to the iconic HBO show set in Baltimore. Then, the Panthers shared a graphic of a panther standing over a Ravens helmet with the caption: "Charming," a reference to Baltimore's nickname as the "Charm City." They also wrote "nevermore" on the bottom in a nod to Edgar Allen Poe's "The Raven" poem where the raven featured repeats: "nevermore." Dallas Cowboys 50, Tennessee Titans 31 A 50-burger wasn't enough for the Dallas Cowboys , who rubbed salt in the Tennessee Titans ' wounds postgame. Dallas scored a touchdown on its first six possessions, the first time that has happened in its franchise history since at least 1978, according to ESPN Research. Cowboys quarterback Dak Prescott provided five of the team's seven touchdowns -- four in the air and one on the ground. Texas and Tennessee are known for their rich histories in country music, but the Cowboys claimed superiority over the Titans by captioning their post: "Texas Country," which has its unique sound. Philadelphia Eagles 19, Pittsburgh Steelers 16 The Philadelphia Eagles held on to defeat the Pittsburgh Steelers at home, ending a seven-game winless streak. Philadelphia put up 13 points in the first quarter, pacing it the rest of the game as Pittsburgh's offense struggled. The Steelers finally found the end zone with 1:20 left in the fourth, but it was too little, too late. They couldn't stop the Eagles on their ensuing drive and Philadelphia survived to win. Held at Lincoln Financial Field, it was an in-state matchup between Pennsylvania's two squads. The Eagles claimed Pennsylvania with a postgame caption that read: "Our State" in all-caps with an image of linebacker Jalyx Hunt on his knees pointing to the sky and Steelers quarterback Aaron Rodgers in the background.

stories.title: Commanders building momentum, halt Bengals' 5-game win streak
stories.summary: The Commanders' defense held the potent Bengals in check and Washington has won three of four.
stories.detailText: LANDOVER, Md. -- The Washington Commanders needed a win to keep pace in the NFC East. They not only got a win, their defense made a statement. The Commanders upset the Cincinnati Bengals 22-20 on a last-second 28-yard field goal by Drew Stevens to win their second game in a row and third in their last four. It's the first time they've won consecutive games since the 2024 season. Quarterback Jayden Daniels needed only two passes -- 23 yards and 42 yards into tight windows -- to lead the Commanders into field goal position. They improved to 4-5-1. A loss would have dropped them three games behind the first-place New York Giants in the NFC East. Though Daniels led the final drive, it was the defense that kept the Commanders around all night. It held the NFL's hottest offense to only 20 points and continued its improved play. With a game next week against Arizona, the Commanders have a chance to get to .500. Here are the most important things to know for both teams: Washington Commanders (4-5-1) Trend to watch: Running back Jacory Croskey-Merritt returned from a groin injury and provided a boost. He carried the ball 13 times for 54 yards and caught two passes for 23 yards. In his previous outing before getting hurt, he gained 82 yards on 11 carries. Most surprising performance: Washington's defense was outstanding. Joe Burrow entered having completed 21 of his last 22 passes vs. the blitz, but the Commanders never shied from that tactic: He was 8-of-16 for 59 yards Monday. They also limited receivers Tee Higgins and Ja'Marr Chase , holding them to a combined seven catches for 74 yards and a touchdown. What to make of the QB performance: Jayden Daniels is getting more and more comfortable. The QB showed his dynamic ability on a 47-yard run. He finished with 289 yards passing and 55 rushing. He kept his eyes upfield on a 29-yard pass off a scramble. Daniels overcame a sluggish start with 85 yards passing at halftime. -- John Keim Next game: Sunday at Arizona Cardinals , 4:25 p.m. ET, Fox Cincinnati Bengals (7-3) Things looked promising for Cincinnati early on Monday night. But the momentum the Bengals built, both in the game and during a five-game winning streak, was halted in a loss to the Commanders. Cincinnati was ineffective on both sides of the ball in the second half. Washington scored on six straight drives, including the game-winning field goal as time expired. The Bengals' offense stalled out late in the contest and couldn't curb the Commanders' surge at Northwest Stadium. Trend to watch: Bengals edge rusher Boye Mafe has been on a roll recently. He had three sacks in the first half alone, making him the first player this season to achieve that feat. Mafe has had a sack in six of his past seven games. Most surprising performance: Rookie tight end Jack Endries had three catches coming into Week 11. By the middle of the fourth quarter, he already had four and he finished with four for 33 yards. Joe Burrow did a good job of finding the underneath options, which included the seventh-round draft pick out of Texas. Stat to know: Cincinnati has taken a ton of pride in its ability to pass the ball with a relative disregard for the running game, given that success through the air. But on a rainy night in Maryland, the Bengals struggled on the ground. Cincinnati had just 31 rushing yards on 14 attempts. -- Ben Baby Next game: Sunday vs. New Orleans Saints , 1 p.m. ET, CBS

stories.detailText: LANDOVER, Md. -- — Jayden Daniels connected with rookie Antonio Williams on two long pass plays, moving the Commanders 64 yards in 34 seconds to set up Drew Stevens’ 26-yard field goal as time expired, and the Washington Commanders stunned Joe Burrow and the Cincinnati Bengals 22-20 on Monday night. After Evan McPherson put the Bengals ahead 20-19 on a 56-yard field goal , Washington got the ball back with 39 seconds left and no timeouts. Daniels hit Williams over the middle for 22 yards, spiked the ball, then found him again for a 42-yard catch-and-run to the Cincinnati 8. The QB spiked it with 5 seconds left and Stevens did the rest. Daniels finished with 283 yards passing, Williams had nine catches for 122 yards, and Stevens was 5 for 5 on field goals as Washington (4-5-1) remained in the NFC East race, two games behind the division-leading New York Giants . Burrow threw for 300 yards and two touchdowns for AFC North-leading Cincinnati (7-3), but the Commanders largely held in check a Bengals team that had won five straight, scoring 31 points or more each time. Washington's defense forced Burrow to settle for checkdowns all night. The dangerous Bengals receiving duo of Ja’Marr Chase and Tee Higgins combined for just seven catches for 74 yards. Washington coach Dan Quinn made another questionable late-game decision when he sent Stevens out on fourth-and-1 to kick a 41-yard field goal with 2:26 left for a 19-17 lead. That left plenty of time for Burrow, who found Mike Gesicki for a 32-yard completion to move the Bengals into field goal range. A sack pushed the Bengals back, but McPherson nailed the long kick with 46 seconds remaining. The game got off to a slow start in rainy conditions but opened up in the second half as the teams traded scores throughout the third quarter. Burrow's 4-yard touchdown pass to Colbie Young put the Bengals ahead 17-10, and the Commanders rallied with three field goals by Stevens. There was an unexpected stoppage early in the third when the stadium lights went out with the Commanders in the red zone. After a delay that lasted about four minutes, Stevens converted from 36 yards to tie the game at 10-all. Washington held Cincinnati to three points on its first four drives before Higgins' 31-yard touchdown catch that made it 10-0. Jacory Croskey-Merritt , activated off injured reserve earlier Monday, scored on a 1-yard run for the Commanders with 12 seconds left before halftime. Injuries Bengals: Safety Bryan Cook suffered a right ankle injury but returned to the game. Up next Bengals: Host the New Orleans Saints on Sunday. Commanders: Visit the Arizona Cardinals on Sunday. ------ See AP’s full NFL coverage here

stories.title: The Bills have a new path to the one seed after the Bengals’ loss
stories.summary: There is a new scenario where the Bills can clinch the AFC’s one seed now that the Bengals lost.
stories.detailText: MINNEAPOLIS, MINNESOTA - NOVEMBER 9: Maxwell Hairston #1 of the Buffalo Bills celebrates after a play during the third quarter against the Minnesota Vikings at U.S. Bank Stadium on November 9, 2026 in Minneapolis, Minnesota. (Photo by Kevin Sabitus/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Buffalo Bills took care of business against an underdog on Sunday, beating the Miami Dolphins. The Jacksonville Jaguars and Cincinnati Bengals both lost to underdogs from the NFC East on Sunday and Monday, which paves the way for the Bills to clinch the number one seed in a new scenario. Yes, with seven games left it is premature to talk about clinching scenarios, but the Bills have a four-game lead in the AFC East plus two games left against the Jets and Dolphins. The division crown is heavily tilted toward the Bills now, and we are starting to look past that to the one seed. (The Bills are obvously focused one game at a time.) With the Jaguars and Bengals losing this week, the Bills now can win the rest of their AFC games and secure the overall record and the AFC record they would need to clinch the one seed, a status that has eluded them throughout Josh Allen’s entire career. Buffalo has games against the Kansas City Chiefs, Denver Broncos, and New England Patriots plus the Dolphins and Jets. Winning those five AFC contests gets them to 14 wins and an 11-1 AFC record with head-to-head tiebreakers over the Broncos and Chiefs. Denver and KC would both have three losses on account of losing to Buffalo. Meanwhile the Jaguars and Bengals could top out at 14-3 but have two AFC losses apiece. Even in a three-way tie scenario, the Bills would come out on top. In short, if the Bills win the rest of their AFC games, they can lose both games to the NFC North’s Chicago Bears and Green Bay Packers and still be the one seed in the AFC. (Winning those is preferable, but irrelevant here.) If the Bills stumble against an AFC opponent, obviously things will need to be recalibrated. Regardless, the Bengals’ loss on Monday is a win for the Bills. AFC playoff standings after Week 11 1. Buffalo Bills (9-1) 2. Denver Broncos (8-2, 4-0 vs KC common opponents) 3. Jacksonville Jaguars (7-3, win over CIN) 4. Cincinnati Bengals (7-3, loss to JAX) 5. Kansas City Chiefs (8-2, 3-1 vs DEN common opponents) 6. Cleveland Browns (6-4, 2-1 AFCN) 7. Pittsburgh Steelers (6-4, AFCN 2-2) 8. New England Patriots (5-5) 9. Houston Texans (4-6) 10. Las Vegas Raiders (4-7) 11. Baltimore Ravens (4-7) 12. New York Jets (3-8, 3-5 AFC) 13. Indianapolis Colts (3-8, 2-6 AFC) 14. Los Angeles Chargers (1-9, 1-6 AFC) 15. Tennessee Titans (1-9, 1-6 AFC) 16. Miami Dolphins (1-9, 1-6 AFC) In the AFC West, the tiebreaker is the record vs common opponents now that they have the same division record. The Broncos are 4-0 against the Raiders, Chargers, Seahawks, and Cardinals. The Chiefs are 3-1 against the same opponents.
