stories.title: NFL Power Rankings entering Week 12: Is it time to start taking the Giants seriously?
stories.summary: The Giants' upset win over the Jaguars changes things. It boosts their chances of making the playoffs as a division champion.
stories.detailText: NFC East: Cowboys | Giants | Eagles | Commanders NFC North : Bears | Lions | Packers | Vikings NFC South: Falcons | Panthers | Saints | Buccaneers NFC West: Cardinals | Rams | 49ers | Seahawks AFC East: Bills | Dolphins | Patriots | Jets AFC North: Ravens | Bengals | Browns | Steelers AFC South: Texans | Colts | Jaguars | Titans AFC West: Broncos | Chiefs | Raiders | Chargers Before Week 11, the New York Giants had a perception problem. They hadn't beaten a team with a winning record. Their advanced metrics said they were a below-average team. Their point differential was +7, which was meager for a 5-3-1 team. They looked like a team lucky to be playing in the putrid NFC East. Then on Sunday, the Giants got a win that can help legitimize their start . They beat a Jaguars team that was a major buyer at the trade deadline and looked like one of the NFL's elite teams . It was easily the Giants' biggest win this season, and for a team that has missed the playoffs eight of the past nine seasons, one of their biggest victories in many years. It might change what is being said about the Giants. "We don't really worry about that, we don't really care what they think or what they say," Giants head coach John Harbaugh said after the game, via the team's transcripts. "It's not our concern how we're evaluated. It's our concern how we play." Yet, they knew what was being said about them. "They keep saying we can't beat these teams, we can't beat them. I don't know why they're saying that," edge rusher Abdul Carter said, according to Yahoo Sports' Jori Epstein . "But what are they going to say now?" The Giants' upset win over the Jaguars changes things. It boosts their chances of making the playoffs as a division champion. The way the Giants' defense played, holding the Jaguars without a touchdown for the first three quarters, gives hope of a strong finish to the year after a first half of the season that lacked a quality win. The offense is still not great, ranking 22nd in DVOA. But J.J. McCarthy makes a few plays each game that also provide some optimism, Malik Nabers is one of the NFL's best receivers, Isaiah Likely is having a breakout season and Cam Skattebo generally provides at least a reasonable run game. The Giants likely aren't going to challenge the 49ers or whoever wins the NFC North for a Super Bowl spot. But their start to the season has more weight behind it after beating a good team. Here are the NFL power rankings after Week 11: 1. San Francisco 49ers (9-1, Last week: 2) The 49ers have faced the No. 1 defense in DVOA (Seattle) and the No. 1 defense in EPA allowed per play (Minnesota). They scored 32 points against the Seahawks and 35 against the Vikings. They got a defensive touchdown in each game but it seems like no defense can hold down the 49ers this season. While the offense has been fantastic, the 49ers wouldn't be the best team in football through Week 11 without their defense, which has excelled despite Nick Bosa not having a sack all season (he did have two quarterback hits on Sunday night). The 49ers have given up 17 or fewer points in six of their 10 games. They have given up fewer than 300 yards in six games too. Defensive coordinator Raheem Morris, who replaced Robert Saleh, is doing an excellent job. 2. Buffalo Bills (9-1, LW: 3) The Bills have given up 37 points in four games since their bye. Of course, they have faced an incredibly fortunate run of backup quarterbacks, including Joe Fagnano, Carson Wentz, Cade Klubnik (who replaced an injured Geno Smith in the second half) and Kyle McCord. Still, they have not given up a touchdown in 43 straight drives, the longest streak during a season since the 2019 Patriots, according to the Bills' site . That makes the Thanksgiving primetime matchup against Patrick Mahomes and the Chiefs one that will help shape this NFL season. Is the Bills' defensive improvement real or because of facing inept quarterbacks? The Bills' defense struggled early, allowing at least 29 points in five of Buffalo's first six games. The only team to not reach 29 points was the Chargers, who are currently 1-9. But the Bills felt like they weren't far off. "When teams were scoring on us, I felt like we were playing good ball," Bills defensive end Greg Rousseau said, via the team's site . "We just had to clean up a couple things here and there. We were playing good ball. We weren't really finishing games at the end of the games." 3. Chicago Bears (8-2, LW: 5) The Bears haven't trailed in five straight games, and that streak brings back memories of the greatest team in franchise history. The last time the Bears went five games without trailing was 1985, when they went the final three games of the regular season and the first two playoff games without trailing, according to Larry Mayer of ChicagoBears.com . The Bears briefly trailed the Patriots 3-0 in Super Bowl XX before winning 46-10. While this version of the Bears is much different than the famous 1985 team, their pass rush is starting to emerge since Jeffery Simmons came aboard in a trade. On Sunday, they sacked the Saints' Tyler Shough six times (three times by Simmons) and had 24 pressures, which is the most for the team since 2018, according to Next Gen Stats . The defensive improvement will be tested on Thanksgiving in a massive NFC North game against the Lions. 4. Jacksonville Jaguars (7-3, LW: 1) Very good teams are allowed to lose games, even ones in which they're favored. But the teams now ahead of them in the rankings haven't taken many losses, and now the Jaguars have three after a miserable performance in a defeat to the Giants on Sunday . Their chances to get the No. 1 seed in the AFC dropped to 1.6% after Sunday, according to DVOA . The Jaguars can rightfully complain that a questionable call cost Parker Washington a touchdown . But the offensive issues for the first three quarters are what ultimately cost them the game. The Jaguars, whose offense had been very good before Sunday, had just one drive longer than 23 yards in the first three quarters and didn't score a touchdown. Jaguars head coach Liam Coen took responsibility, saying his plan "maybe had too many things in, moving parts." "That's a direct reflection of me, and making sure that these guys are prepared well enough," Coen said, via the team's site . "We had been prepared in the majority of our football games, I felt like, and that did not show tonight, especially early on. I put that directly on me." 5. Kansas City Chiefs (8-2, LW: 7) The Chiefs scored on all five of their first-half drives against the Cardinals, quickly putting away a poor and injured team. One of the stars of the game was tight end Travis Kelce, who is having a remarkable season at age 37. He has 586 yards and four touchdowns, two of which came Sunday against Arizona . His 58.6 yards per game is his most since 2023. There were only three instances of a tight end having more than 400 yards at age 37, and Kelce is already second on that list behind Tony Gonzalez and his 859 yards in 2013. Kelce is on pace for 996 yards. There were conversations that Kelce could retire after each of the past two seasons, but he's still one of the most productive tight ends in the game. That helps a Chiefs offense that is fourth in EPA per play. 6. Denver Broncos (8-2, LW: 8) It was a typical Broncos win and not the blowout the 38-24 score indicates. They were outgained 370-351 by the Raiders. Las Vegas rallied to tie the game at 17 after falling behind 17-0 and had the ball at the two-minute warning, down seven points. A pick-6 by Ja'Quan McMillian put the game away in the Broncos' favor. The best part of the win for the Broncos was perhaps finding an offensive identity. Rookie Jonah Coleman has taken over the backfield, and he had 111 yards and three touchdowns on 24 rushing attempts Sunday. "It's not easy, but he's responded really well to his situation," quarterback Bo Nix said, according to the team's transcripts. "He's been given a great opportunity with RJ Harvey getting hurt (knee) and having a few weeks off. ... It was an impressive performance getting that many carries, running the ball hard." 7. Cincinnati Bengals (7-3, LW: 4) The Bengals have leaned into being a one-dimensional offense, and it hurt them on Monday. The Commanders got consistent pressure on Joe Burrow, including on some well-timed blitzes, and that was partially because they didn’t have to worry at all about Cincinnati’s running game. The Bengals rushed 14 times for 31 yards and threw it 40 times. When the Bengals got into field-goal range in the final two minutes, they couldn’t run for a first down to grind out the remainder of the clock. They passed on second and third downs and couldn’t pick it up. That allowed the Commanders 46 seconds, which they used to drive for a game-winning field goal. The Bengals should lean on Burrow, who is still tracking to win an MVP after 300 yards and two touchdowns on Monday night. But the lack of a running game, and even the lack of any attempt to try it, could be a big problem for the Bengals in the playoffs. 8. Detroit Lions (8-2, LW: 11) Detroit's first defensive test without Aidan Hutchinson went well. The Lions allowed just 274 yards and 21 points, and Tampa Bay got 65 yards and a touchdown on a meaningless drive at the end of a game when Detroit led by 17 points. The Lions had four sacks, which was a good sign. The Lions' defense has been much better since the first few weeks of the season, and Sunday's game was without Hutchinson and linebacker Jack Campbell. The test Thursday will be tougher, with the Chicago Bears coming in with first place in the NFC North on the line. But if Detroit's defense can maintain this level, the Lions might be a Super Bowl contender. That could reveal itself on Thanksgiving. "Our guys are competitive, man, and they don't want to be counted out," Lions head coach Dan Campbell said of the defense's performance Sunday, via the team's site . "And nobody cares. There are no excuses. And the only way to gain respect is just go about your business, man, and make plays and play together and prove your worth, man." 9. Minnesota Vikings (7-3, LW: 6) What we learned about the Vikings on Sunday night, mostly, was that the 49ers are on a much different tier . That's OK, because the 49ers are on a higher tier than all but a few teams. The blitz was impervious to the 49ers' offense. Minnesota blitzed on 88.9% of San Francisco's dropbacks, and Brock Purdy was 19-of-23 passing for 231 yards and two touchdowns on those plays, according to Pro Football Focus . "It's one of those things where I told our team, you know, when you play a good team like that and you don't play your best, you're going to get beat," Vikings head coach Kevin O'Connell said, according to the team's site . That hadn't happened before to the Vikings' defense and is unlikely to repeat, but now Minnesota has to adjust after its worst defensive day of the season. 10. Seattle Seahawks (6-4, LW: 9) The NFC West race is probably over, with the 49ers leading it by three games, but Seattle has a shot to make it interesting. The Seahawks play at the 49ers in Week 12 and there's an opportunity to at least make the race interesting. The big story will be Sam Darnold, whether he can return from injury and how well he plays. The Seahawks are not entertaining the idea of replacing him with Drew Lock. Seahawks head coach Mike Macdonald defended Darnold, pointing out that he has been injured for most of the season, starting with the first game. "The beginning of the year for Sam has been a tough road," Macdonald said on Seattle Sports 710, via the team's site . "I can't wait for him to be fully healthy, probably for the first time — minimal times it's happened this year — and get a full week's worth of work and we'll rock and roll from there." 11. Los Angeles Rams (6-4, LW: 10) The dream of getting Puka Nacua back for a playoff run is dead, after Nacua had knee surgery that will keep him out the rest of the season . Davante Adams should return but the Rams' offense won't be what was expected before the season, when expectations were sky high. Even making the playoffs will be difficult because of the Rams' challenging upcoming schedule. Their playoff odds are down to 38.1%, according to DVOA . The Rams practically need a win Wednesday over the Packers, who are one of their main competitors in a very tough NFC wild-card race. 12. Green Bay Packers (6-4, LW: 12) Micah Parsons is set to return for the Packers after practicing in pads Sunday. It's major news for Green Bay to add one of the NFL's best players to the lineup. The Packers were 9-3-1 and leading in the second half at Denver when Parsons tore his ACL last season. Wednesday at the Rams is a massive game for the Packers and their playoff hopes, and there will be the temptation to play Parsons more than he's ready for in his return. Packers head coach Matt LaFleur is aware of that issue. "I never wanna place limitations on anybody, but he hasn't played football in a long time," LaFleur said, via Athlon Sports . "So, I think you've got to be conscious of that, and there's probably going to be plays that don't look like him, and there's going to be some plays that do." 13. New York Giants (6-3-1, LW: 16) Perhaps the biggest development for the Giants on Sunday was defensive end Abdul Carter picking up two sacks. Production had been surprisingly thin for the third overall pick of the 2025 NFL Draft. He had just six sacks in 26 games before Sunday, though his underlying metrics said that sacks were bound to come. Carter also had five quarterback hits. Carter came in as an elite prospect and if he can start translating his pass rush success into sacks, that could be huge for the Giants. That happened Sunday as the defense played very well against a good Jaguars offense. "As a defense, we showed what we really about," Carter told CBS after the game . "And for me, I'm the best in the world." 14. Cleveland Browns (6-4, LW: 14) Seeing the Raiders' upset bid fall short was good news for the Browns. Their game against Las Vegas in Week 12, which got flexed to Sunday night, would have been much more interesting in the wild-card race had the Raiders been 5-6 instead of 4-7. It also wasn't bad for Cleveland to see the Steelers slip back to 6-4 with a bad loss at Philadelphia . The Browns aren't a lock to make the playoffs but the path is very clear. They have two games left against the Bengals and one against the Giants, but the other four are against teams with losing records. 15. Carolina Panthers (5-5, LW: 17) The biggest game in the NFC South this season comes in Tampa Bay next Monday night. The Panthers face the Buccaneers. Tampa Bay gets the season sweep and the tiebreaker with the win. The Falcons and Saints aren't completely out of the running, but Carolina and Tampa Bay look like the two best teams in a bad division. An old problem popped up again, and it was the run defense. Baltimore had 157 rushing yards, averaging 7.1 yards per attempt. That's a bad weakness to have against the Buccaneers, who lead the NFL at 5 yards per carry. "They had way too many yards today. Takeaways and stuff is cool, but we got to stop them in the run game," linebacker Tyrel Dodson told the team's site . 16. Pittsburgh Steelers (6-4, LW: 13) The Steelers were showing improvement but the last two weeks are alarming. They were destroyed by the Bengals, then didn't threaten an Eagles team that had lost seven in a row and was on its third quarterback this season. The lingering problem from the game is receiver DK Metcalf getting ejected after another unproductive game. The NFL reportedly won't suspend him , but that doesn't mean Pittsburgh can rely on a player who hasn't done much on the field and whose behavior is unreliable too. There are also injury concerns at a key spot. Edge rusher Nick Herbig was inactive Sunday because of rib and hip injuries, then Alex Highsmith left the game against the Eagles early because of an ankle injury. The Steelers get the 8-2 Broncos on Friday and the Texans and Jaguars after that. Pittsburgh was once 6-2. It's possible it will be under .500 by mid-December. 17. Houston Texans (4-6, LW: 18) David Montgomery could finally make a big impact for the Texans. In his return from injury, he rushed for 107 yards on 26 carries against the Colts. Indianapolis isn't a good team but it was still nice to see something positive from Houston's running game, even if it was in a blowout. The Texans have been looking for consistency all season, but it's not too late for them to rally for a wild-card spot in a weak race. Their Week 13 game at the Steelers will be a big one for the Texans' playoff hopes. For now, Houston hopes a dominant win over Indianapolis is the start of a streak. "It's huge," quarterback C.J. Stroud said, according to the team's site . "I think this is a start to something that we need to go on a run with." 18. Washington Commanders (4-5-1, LW: 20) Jayden Daniels is still capable of looking like a superstar at quarterback. When the Commanders looked like they had lost to the Bengals on a field goal with 46 seconds left, Daniels hit two passes to rookie Antonio Williams for a total of 64 yards, which set up a game-winning field goal as time expired. They were two great throws from Daniels and a great job by Williams to get open. Daniels finished with 289 yards, 122 of which went to Williams. The Commanders are 4-5-1, which is still two games behind the Giants in the NFC East. But Daniels and Williams kept the Commanders’ season alive with two great plays in the final minute on Monday night. 19. Tampa Bay Buccaneers (3-7, LW: 15) Baker Mayfield's injuries have played a big part in his quiet season, but the Buccaneers still need more from the passing game. Mayfield's top game this season is 243 yards. He had 187 yards against a vulnerable Lions defense on Sunday. Mayfield has just five passing touchdowns in 175 attempts. His yards per attempt of 6.3 is the lowest of his career. Mayfield was playing through a foot injury Sunday. The Buccaneers need more out of the passing game because they can't keep dropping games and stay in the NFC South race. A loss Monday night to the Panthers might ruin their playoff hopes. "We're out of mulligans," Mayfield said, according to the team's site. 20. Dallas Cowboys (5-6, LW: 22) It's weird to say after giving up 30 points at home to the Titans, but the Cowboys' defense did look better after Mike Pettine took over play-calling duties from Christian Parker. Almost all of the Titans' yards came when they were down double digits and trying to get back in the game. The Titans didn't score a touchdown in the first half. "Very proud of those guys," Cowboys head coach Brian Schottenheimer said of the defense, according to the team's site . "I think the first half was outstanding, but I thought they did a great job of blocking out the noise and working. I was really excited for how they performed." 21. Las Vegas Raiders (4-7, LW: 19) Fernando Mendoza played well, although his pick-6 in the fourth quarter with the game on the line was a rookie moment. Against a very good Broncos defense, Mendoza had 267 yards and three touchdowns. He also rushed for 22 yards. He played well despite being without superstar tight end Brock Bowers, who was out with an ankle injury. For a second NFL start, it was promising. "He's a first-round pick, first overall for a reason," Broncos linebacker Alex Singleton said, via the team's transcripts. "He's going to be a good player." The pick-6 just after the two-minute warning ended the Raiders' comeback hopes, but there was still obvious progress from Mendoza. "I felt a lot more comfortable this week than last week," Mendoza said, via the team's site . "They're both great defenses, both top in the league. However, I just felt like I was able to settle in and was able to see the entire field better. I was able to see the entire football field. 22. New England Patriots (5-5, LW: 21) Daniel Jones could remain an option for the Patriots after he was suddenly released by the Colts, though coach Mike Vrabel wouldn't address that on Monday. He said Tommy DeVito will start in Week 12. "We're excited about that, good preseason, and Tommy's improved," Vrabel said . DeVito struggled badly when he was forced into action against the Lions in Germany before the bye week. He gets to face the Chargers this week, which gives DeVito a chance to impress and keep the job. But it also wouldn't be surprising if Jones finishes the season for a Patriots team that is still in the playoff race. 23. Baltimore Ravens (4-7, LW: 23) Years from now, people will look back on the 2026 Ravens, see that Lamar Jackson missed most of the season and attribute Baltimore's poor record to that. And it won't be completely accurate. The defense, which is head coach Jesse Minter's specialty, has been miserable. Over the Ravens' last five games they have allowed 35, 36, 33, 23 and 35 points. Baltimore lost all five of those games, and its losing streak it at six. Minter took the blame for the Panthers putting together a game-winning drive late in the fourth quarter, saying "It was just a poor job by me, and that's what it was." Players disagreed. "I wouldn't necessarily agree with it, truthfully," linebacker Roquan Smith told the team's site . "I thought we were in some really good calls. It comes down to us doing our job. That has been the story all season." The responsibility for a bad season still falls on Minter, who is in his first season as a head coach. Baltimore is 26th in the NFL in points allowed. 24. New Orleans Saints (3-7, LW: 24) The Saints really don't do anything well. They're 21st in points scored and 22nd in yards gained, 23rd in points allowed and 27th in points allowed. They're 16th in passing yards, 18th in passing yards allowed, 28th in rushing yards and 28th in rushing yards allowed. Even the passing yardage is not that great; Tyler Shough's yards per attempt of 6.2 is better than only four of the 32 qualified quarterbacks this season. Up and down their résumé, there's nothing that stands out as a strength. It has been a dreadful follow-up to a good second half to last season, which provided some false hope for the Saints heading into this season. It looks like a multiple-year rebuild is still in the beginning stages. The good news is the Saints would have the eighth overall pick of the draft if the season ended now. 25. Atlanta Falcons (3-7, LW: 25) The problem with the Falcons isn't even their record, because they play in the NFC South. But the upcoming schedule is at Vikings, vs. Lions and at Browns. Even one win in those three puts them at 4-9 with four to go. Atlanta will have to play a lot better to stay alive in the playoff hunt over the next three games. The Falcons had a great two-game stretch against the Packers and Saints and also are the only team to beat the 49ers, so figuring out why they can't play that way most weeks has been tough. "We got really good players, man," Falcons running back Bijan Robinson said, via the team's site . "Obviously, with the good players, you have to execute at a high level. We have to come together this week and tell ourselves, 'Is this how we want to end the season?'" 26. Philadelphia Eagles (3-7, LW: 30) Sunday wasn't a perfect game for the Eagles, with just 214 yards on offense, but the defense is starting to play well. It allowed 255 yards in the win over Pittsburgh, the second time in a row they've held an opponent under 300 yards. Before that stretch, the Eagles hadn't held an opponent to fewer than 300 yards since Week 2, which was the last time Philadelphia had won a game before Sunday. The Eagles' defense will be tested against a very good Cowboys offense that is coming off a 50-point game against the Titans. But seeing the defense come through, with stellar linebacker play from Jeremiah Trotter Jr. and Jihaad Campbell and five sacks, gives them some hope for a happy Thanksgiving. 27. New York Jets (3-8, LW: 31) The Jets have little to play for, and a loss to the Chargers would have put them in much better draft position next April, but winning is good for any NFL locker room. Even if it's against the Chargers. "The thing is, a win is a win and that's what we look for and that's the way you play this game," Jets coach Aaron Glenn said, according to the team's site . There have been some promising developments in the Jets' season, and probably none bigger than the play of edge rusher David Bailey, the second overall pick of the draft. Bailey had two more sacks, giving him 9.5 for the season. Jevon Kearse set the rookie record with 14.5 and Bailey is on pace to break that, though in a 17-game season. He has been undeniably impressive and a big piece for a Jets team that has three first-round picks next year. 28. Arizona Cardinals (3-8, LW: 26) Nick Rallis always seemed like a bit of an awkward fit as the Cardinals' defensive coordinator, considering he wasn't successful in three previous seasons under an old regime but was retained. First-year coach Mike LaFleur fired him Monday after another disappointing performance. The Cardinals are 31st in expected points added allowed per play, ahead of only the Cowboys. The Cardinals haven't been good on defense, but talent certainly seems to lack. Safety Budda Baker, the one star the defense has, leads the team with 3.5 sacks. That's a terrible sign. First-round picks up front, like Zaven Collins and Darius Robinson, haven't broken out. We're about to find out if that was because of a coaching problem. 29. Indianapolis Colts (3-8, LW: 27) The Colts cutting Daniel Jones less than 24 hours after his 11th straight start to begin the season was odd, even if it ensures the Colts don't have to pay a 2027 injury guarantee. Jones was poor against the Texans, but he was poor all season. He's dead last among NFL starting quarterbacks in EPA per play this season. But the Colts didn't care before Week 11, starting Jones and seemingly never giving any serious consideration to benching him to at least get a look at Anthony Richardson Sr. Cutting a quarterback after starting him all season is a sign of a franchise that isn't making sound decisions. At least the Colts now can get a look at Richardson, who did show some progress in the preseason. Richardson hasn't shown many signs that he can be an NFL starter, but it's not like the Colts are losing anything by taking another look. 30. Miami Dolphins (1-9, LW: 28) The Dolphins have nine losses already but haven't been thoroughly dominated often. They were dominated on Sunday, when they fell behind early and got crushed by a superior Bills team. One positive point from Sunday was another big game from rookie linebacker Jacob Rodriguez, who had 13 tackles and an interception. He has 93 tackles, a pair of interceptions and a sack this season. Rodriguez was a tremendous college player but he fell to the second round of the NFL Draft. He has already shown his college production was no fluke and gives the Dolphins one foundational piece in what is going to be a long rebuild. 31. Tennessee Titans (1-9, LW: 29) There wasn't much to be happy with after Sunday's blowout loss. Cam Ward's final line didn't look terrible, but in the first half against a Cowboys defense that is worst in the NFL in many categories, Ward had 55 passing yards and the Titans didn't score a touchdown. The defense was even worse, giving up 51 points. In Tennessee's last four games it has allowed 491, 510, 459 and 480 yards. The defense was supposed to be much better under Robert Saleh, and it is one of the worst in the NFL. Tennessee has allowed more yards per game than any other team. "These last couple of weeks, I'm not going to try and sugar-coat anything," Saleh said Monday, according to the team's site . "It's been dog sh**." 32. Los Angeles Chargers (1-9, LW: 32) Good thing the Chargers got that one win. Losing to the Jets on Sunday at home was a strong indication that Los Angeles might not win again. At least there were a couple decent performances on offense. Omarion Hampton continued to get hot late in the season with 89 rushing yards. Justin Herbert had a 119.3 passer rating. His best mark in a game this season before Sunday was 87.5. Unfortunately, Herbert landed in concussion protocol after the loss. Ladd McConkey has had an injury-filled and unproductive season but he had two touchdowns against the Jets. It's not much, especially in a loss. But it's not like there have been many other positives for the Chargers.

As ESPN rules analyst Russell Yurk explained in the postgame show, the clock operator incorrectly ran the remaining four seconds off the clock during the game-winning field goal from Washington. Yurk said two seconds remained when the ball hit the net. It looks more like it should have been one second. Regardless, Yurk said the replay process can't restore time when the next play isn't a scrimmage play. (There's also a rule regarding restoring time when there are fewer than two seconds left, and — with all due respect to Yurk — it appears that there was only one second when the ball hit the net.) The bottom line is that the clock operator was slow to get to the button, and there wasn't anything that could be done about it. What would have happened if the Bengals had gotten one last chance? We'll never know, because the person hired to keep track of the time handled it incorrectly. Or, depending on that person's rooting interests, he handled it perfectly.

stories.title: As Commanders stay in playoff race, Bengals' rivals rejoice: MNF winners and losers
stories.summary: While the Commanders kept their postseason hopes alive with a last-second win on "Monday Night Football," the Bengals' playoff standing weakened.
stories.detailText: LANDOVER, MD – On a drizzly, breezy night outside the nation's capital, the Washington Commanders put a damper on the Cincinnati Bengals five-game winning streak, prevailing 22-20 on Monday, Nov. 23, as Drew Stevens' fifth field goal of the night at the final gun provided the winning margin. Not only did the Commanders wind up victorious , they executed to perfection in a late-game situation − a scenario that had been a major bugaboo throughout the season prior to their upset of the Stripes. As with almost any NFL game, there is plenty to sift through on a night with several winners and losers beyond the final score registered at the end. They are as follows: WINNERS Jayden Daniels and Antonio Williams The third-year quarterback and rookie wideout, respectively, hooked up twice for 64 yards in the game's frenetic final drive, which spanned 46 seconds. Commanders' playoff chances At 3-5-1, they remain two games behind the New York Giants in the NFC East but have the tiebreaker if they can catch them. Drew Stevens The undrafted rookie kicker out of Iowa shrugged off the elements to do the bulk of the scoring for Washington − perfect on all five of his field-goal tries and one PAT to account for 16 of the Commanders' 22 points. He drilled the game-winning 26-yarde on the game's final play. Boye Mafe Trey who? The Cincinnati edge rusher, who entered the night with a team-leading 6½ sacks, bagged Washington QB Jayden Daniels three times – leaving Mafe among the league’s top five in that department by night’s end. Boye Mafe could not be stopped in the 1st half. He is the 1st player with 3 sacks in the 1st half of a Monday Night Football game since Connor Barwin in 2014. 🤯 pic.twitter.com/ofgluFfJZF — ESPN Insights (@ESPNInsights) November 24, 2026 Joe Buck and Troy Aikman As speculation continues to swirl about the "Monday Night Football" tandem ’s partnership – and specifically the fate of apparent lame duck Aikman – the duo continue to deliver a professional broadcast every week that belies the apparent tension that exists behind the scenes and that the Hall of Fame quarterback continues to fuel when he’s interviewed by other outlets between games. ‘The Hail Raiser’ It certainly wasn’t a neutral voting party, but 100% of the three dozen tailgaters polled by USA TODAY Sports at Northwest Stadium prior to kickoff enthusiastically embraced Washington’s new alternate logo, a gold spear infused through the Commanders’ usual “W” sigil. The mostly black alternate uniform was nearly as popular amid its coming-out party … though Buck said the burgundy jersey numbers were hard to decipher from the “MNF” booth. Pittsburgh Steelers and Cleveland Browns Cincinnati’s loss reduced its lead over its nearest AFC North pursuers to one game while weakening the Bengals’ playoff standing, where they are currently projected as the No. 4 seed. Jacksonville Jaguars Cincinnati’s loss softened the blow of the Jags ’ Sunday loss to the Giants just a bit. By virtue of a superior record in AFC games, Jacksonville reclaimed the third overall spot in the projected AFC postseason field. LOSERS Northwest Stadium lights The field temporarily went dark three minutes into the third quarter – and with NFL commissioner Roger Goodell looking on from a suite. Fortunately, it was never a Super Bowl 47-adjacent situation , and the press box remained fully lit along much of the venue’s secondary lighting, main scoreboard and ribbon panels throughout the interior of the stadium. After a short commercial break from ESPN, the field was again aglow … apparently after the building’s lighting vendor re-enabled the main lights, which usually go down for maintenance on Monday nights. “The lighting vendor never disabled the regularly scheduled maintenance for 10 PM. It’s a weekday thing, and they forgot it was a Monday night game.” – Joe Buck on why the lights went out during Bengals-Commanders pic.twitter.com/vl3QwoJ8Zg — ESPN (@espn) November 24, 2026 Joe Burrow Hardly ideal playing conditions given a slick ball and field, not to mention an inspired effort by Washington’s defense – which prevented the presumed MVP frontrunner from setting an NFL record by accounting for at least four TDs (passing and/or rushing) in six consecutive games. Ja'Marr Chase Cincinnati's receiver had a quiet night (5 catches, 31 yards) and lost the chance to match Hall of Famer Calvin Johnson's mark of snagging at least 10 passes in four consecutive games. stories.title: Rams open to free-agent ‘upgrade’ with just four receivers left on roster
stories.summary: When Sean McVay sends three wide receivers onto the field against the Packers on Wednesday night, he can look down the sideline and find exactly one more.
stories.detailText: When Sean McVay sends three wide receivers onto the field against the Packers on Wednesday night, he can look down the sideline and find exactly one more. That’s where the Rams stand before any practice squad elevations. A veteran who can give Matthew Stafford another dependable target would help. So would a fifth receiver who can spell one of the first four. Los Angeles Rams receiver Puka Nacua (12) celebrates a touchdown with head coach Sean McVay in Landover, Md., Sunday, Nov. 8, 2026. Getty Images Asked Monday whether the Rams would pursue a veteran free agent, McVay said, “We’ve talked about all those types of things,” according to the L.A. Times . So that’s a possibility? “I would never rule out opportunities to upgrade,” McVay said, adding that his current receivers did “a great job” in their last game. There’s room to agree with McVay on both counts. Xavier Smith caught his first NFL touchdown in the win over Arizona. Konata Mumpfield had already shown what he could do in an expanded role, catching four passes for 93 yards and a go-ahead touchdown in Denver while Puka Nacua was sidelined. Both have earned work. The trouble is how few players are behind them. Los Angeles Rams head coach Sean McVay leaves the field after defeating the Las Vegas Raiders at Allegiant Stadium in Las Vegas on Sunday, Oct. 25, 2026. Getty Images Monday’s depth chart lists rookie C.J. Daniels on one side and Tutu Atwell on the other, with Mumpfield in the slot and Smith behind him. Neither outside spot has a backup listed. The Rams have already had to reach outside the organization to get to four. Smith was on San Francisco’s practice squad before Los Angeles brought him back when Jordan Whittington went on injured reserve. At the trade deadline, the Rams had reason to think the numbers would improve. They passed on trading for a receiver in part because they expected Nacua and tight end Terrance Ferguson back this season. San Francisco 49ers wide receivers Deebo Samuel, left, and Brandon Aiyuk take part in an NFL football practice in Santa Clara, Calif., Tuesday, June 6, 2023. AP Nacua has since undergone knee surgery , Ferguson needs season-ending ankle surgery and Davante Adams is still recovering from hamstring surgery . Ferguson’s absence also costs McVay a receiving option when he wants to give one of his wideouts a breather and put another tight end on the field. Spotrac lists Brandin Cooks, Hunter Renfrow and Tyreek Hill among the available veteran receivers. Brandon Aiyuk could join them if he clears waivers after the 49ers waived him Monday, ending a lengthy standoff . Availability on paper only tells the Rams so much. Hill’s agent said earlier this month that the receiver was still awaiting medical clearance, and McVay didn’t single out a target Monday. A practice squad call-up can get the Rams through Wednesday. With seven games left and two expected reinforcements lost for the year, there’s a job here for someone who can stick beyond one game day. stories.title: Monday Night Football: Commanders rally for 22-20 win over Bengals
stories.summary: There were no late mistakes for the Commanders this time.
stories.detailText: The Commanders have wilted in the final moments of games at points this season, but they didn't do so on Monday night. After a 56-yard field goal by Evan McPherson put the Bengals up 20-19, the Commanders took possession on their own 28-yard line with 46 seconds left to play. Jayden Daniels hit rookie wideout Antonio Williams with a pair of passes that covered 64 yards and exorcised the demons from their tie with the Giants by spiking the ball with time left for Drew Stevens to try a 26-yard field goal. Stevens knocked it through the uprights and the Commanders were 22-20 winners on their home field. It's the second straight win for the Commanders and the end of a five-game winning streak for the Bengals. Daniels was 23-of-35 for 289 yards and the Commanders scored on six straight drives after opening the game with four punts on four possessions. The final five of those drives ended with Stevens field goals, but the Commanders dominated time of possession in the final 30 minutes. Their run game had a big hand in that. Jacory Croskey-Merritt had 13 carries for 54 yards and a touchdown and Daniels had a 47-yard run to set up one of Stevens's kicks. Williams led all receivers with nine catches for 122 yards, but the Commanders remained in position to pull out the win thanks to their defense. The Bengals were limited to 124 yards in the second half and they punted twice after taking a 17-10 lead in the third quarter. Joe Burrow finished with 300 passing yards, but the big plays that were the hallmark of their winning streak didn't develop against a Commanders defense that limited Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins to seven catches for 74 yards. Washington improved to 4-5-1 with the win and they have to feel good about their chances of sticking around the NFC East race with games against the Cardinals and Titans on tap in the next two weeks. The Giants finished Week 11 at 6-3-1 and the Cowboys are 5-6. The Bengals are now 7-3, which leaves them a game clear of both the Browns and Steelers in the AFC North. They split their season series with the Steelers and still have both games against the Browns on their upcoming schedule, but their immediate focus will be on next Sunday's game against the Saints.

stories.title: Vikings Football and the Fine Art of Catastrophizing
stories.summary: Because nobody does it like we do
stories.detailText: MEXICO CITY, MEXICO - NOVEMBER 22: Justin Jefferson #18 of the Minnesota Vikings carries the ball against Deommodore Lenoir #2 of the San Francisco 49ers during the third quarter at Estadio Banorte on November 22, 2026 in Mexico City, Mexico. (Photo by Manuel Velasquez/Getty Images) | Getty Images In Week 11, Minnesota Vikings fans waited all day for Sunday Night. . .and almost immediately wished that they hadn’t. In what had been billed as one of the games of the year in the National Football League, the Vikings managed to hang with the San Francisco 49ers for about a quarter and a half before a late second-quarter touchdown pass from Brock Purdy and a pick-six from Kirk Cousins essentially ended things before halftime. The scoreboard said 35-10 at the end of the night, but it was over long before that. Of course, the internet being what it is, there was much weeping and gnashing of teeth and rending of garments and those sorts of things. The euphoria that had washed over Vikings fans following the return of Kirk-a-Mania just a week prior had been swept away and replaced with the lament that Brian Flores’ defense had been “exposed,” and that teams around the league now had the “blueprint” to beat the league’s top defense going forward. Because that’s the way things are now. Everything is either the greatest or the worst. Hell, sometimes things are both of those things simultaneously, somehow. Don’t ask me how it happens, because I don’t know. I’m fifty years old, and everything hurts. . .I can barely walk and chew gum at the same time, let alone reconcile those two things simultaneously. But yes, the Niners put forth a very specific blueprint on Sunday night on how to beat the Vikings’ defense. Step one of that blueprint is, apparently, “Start Brock Purdy at quarterback.” That eliminates a lot of other teams from being able to emulate it. Honestly, that guy is operating on a level that pretty much no other quarterback in the league is currently operating on. I’ll listen to an argument for Joe Burrow, but at this point that’s just about it. He handled Flores’ scheme in a way that nobody has in a very long time. Brock Purdy went 16-for-18 for 195 yards and 2 TDs against the Vikings' blitz. His 88.9% completion percentage was the highest against a Brian Flores blitz since Week 1, 2019 (Lamar Jackson). When pressured on blitzes, Purdy finished 8-for-9 for 100 yards. Powered by @awscloud pic.twitter.com/1KRPL6efDC — Next Gen Stats (@NextGenStats) November 23, 2026 But even if the Niners did put a “blueprint” out there. . .so what? Let me illustrate this with a slightly different example. If you play video games and you get stuck on a specific part of the game, you can pause the game or turn it off, head on over to YouTube, and find no shortage of videos of people showing you everything you need to do in order to get past that one particular spot you’re having trouble with. You can probably even find four or five different people who will show you four or five different strategies to get through exactly the same map or boss or whatever it might be. You can watch all the videos your eyes can handle. Eventually, however, you reach a point where you have to step away from the video, go back to your console, pick up your controller, and do the job yourself. And if your reflexes aren’t fast enough or you hit the wrong button at the wrong time. . .well, that “blueprint” that you got from watching all those videos really doesn’t do you a whole lot of good, does it? Teams can know what they have to do in order to beat the Vikings’ defense all they want. How many teams can actually go out and do it? The Vikings have lost three games so far this season. In two of those three losses, they were competitive until the late stages of the game, despite Kyler Murray and Carson Wentz looking like they had never actually seen a football before, never mind having any idea what the heck they were actually supposed to do with one. In the other one, they happened to run into the one team equipped. . .almost uniquely so. . .to beat them at what they do best. And if the Vikings should happen to meet up with that team again at some point, Flores has earned enough of my trust at this point for me to believe he’s going to make enough changes to not let it happen again. Now. . .while I can understand the disappointment after watching a game like Sunday night’s loss, there’s plenty of reason to be positive about the rest of the season. Am I crazy? Possibly, but that has nothing to do with football. Allow me to explain what I’m talking about as far as the Vikings are concerned. The Vikings have seven games left on the schedule. Only two of those games will be played away from U.S. Bank Stadium. Those will be the Thursday Night Football game in Week 14 at New England and Week 17 at the New York Jets. The Patriots will be without Drake Maye and, as of now, are starting Tommy “In a Gadda” Devito at quarterback. The Jets. . .well, I was always taught that if you can’t say anything nice. . . The Vikings also only have two games remaining against teams with winning records the rest of the way. Both of them are against division opponents, and both of them are at home. Those will be on Sunday Night Football in Week 15 against Detroit (coming off a mini-bye following the New England game), and the regular-season finale against Chicago. The other three games are against Atlanta (currently 3-7), Carolina (currently 5-5), and Washington (currently 4-5-1). According to PlayoffStatus.com , despite currently sitting behind both Detroit and Chicago in the NFC North, the Vikings have the inside track to both the NFC North title and the #2 seed in the NFC playoffs. They also have the second-highest odds of making the playoffs overall in the NFC at 93%. According to Tankathon , in terms of remaining strength of schedule, the Bears, Lions, and Packers rank #1, #5, and #7, respectively. The Vikings rank. . .#16. So the sledding is much tougher for the rest of the division, at least on paper, than it is for the purple. You can make a pretty convincing argument that the Vikings could (should?) be favored in every game they play from here on out. The Lions and Bears play each other on Thanksgiving, so barring a tie, one of them is going to come out of Week 12 with a third loss. The Vikings have swept the Packers already, so Green Bay would need a minor miracle to overtake Minnesota for anything at this point. The bottom line is that there’s still plenty of football to be played, and while, yes, the loss to the Niners was painful to watch, it’s not going to ruin the season or anything. There are adjustments to be made and, hopefully, this team will make them. Now it’s time for them. . .and for us, as fans. . .to get up, dust ourselves off, and get ready for the last seven games of the year, starting with Kirkomecoming (if that’s even a word, and if it’s not, I just made it up) on Sunday afternoon at U.S. Bank Stadium.

stories.title: SEC plans to consider ejecting LSU on December 3
stories.summary: The supposed "chaos" in college sports could still result in the SEC kicking LSU out of the conference.
stories.detailText: {"unknownError":"There has been an error","expiredError":"This video has been expired due to copyright restrictions.","unavailableError":"This content is not yet available.","georestrictedError":"This content is not available in your location.","networkId":"169843","adManagerUrl":"https://mssl.fwmrm.net/libs/adm/6.51.0/AdManager.js","serverId":"https://29773.v.fwmrm.net/ad/g/1","profileId":"169843:nbcu_web_jwp_cs_moat_https","afid":"140315314","caid":"nbcs_nbc_pftpm_protectcollegesports_261121","csid":"nbcsports_embed_on_domain","sfid":"","adHocGroup":"","athlete":"","businessUnit":"NBC Sports","category":"","duration":"663196","event":"","externalAdvertiserId":"nbcs_nbc_pftpm_protectcollegesports_261121","genre":"News","guid":"nbc_pftpm_protectcollegesports_261121","league":"NCAA","network":"","platform":"PC","playlist":"","show":"PFT PM","sport":"Football","subtype":"","team":"","title": "Why the Protect College Sports Act may be 'dead'","datePublished":"","videoPageUrl": "https://www.nbcsports.com/watch/nfl/profootballtalk/pft-pm/why-the-protect-college-sports-act-may-be-dead-in-congress","availableDate":"2026-11-21T19:14:51Z","expirationDate":"","countries":""} The supposed "chaos" in college sports could still result in the SEC kicking LSU out of the conference. Via Mark Schlabach of ESPN, the conference plans to consider giving LSU the boot at a meeting on December 3. The disclosure came in court papers filed Monday in connection with a legal battle arising from LSU's placement of guard RJ Luis Jr. on the roster, after he played in preseason games for the Boston Celtics. "The lawsuit seeks to protect the Conference's ability to govern itself and to enforce the rules and policies its member universities have voluntarily adopted," the SEC said in a statement. "The Conference maintains its right to associate only with institutions that meet its established standards and expectations of membership and that demonstrate appropriate institutional control of their athletics programs." The fight first emerged when the LSU football team considered adding to the roster players who had spots on 90-man NFL rosters in the offseason, training camp, and preseason. LSU eventually backed down. The overriding question is whether players who have signed what are essentially tryout contract are "professional" players. And whether college athletes who are now being paid are not "professional." The entire dynamic arises from players making the strategic decision to pursue opportunities deemed to be more lucrative. College athletes in the high-revenue sports are essentially pro players. The fact that a small handful of players who have attempted to become pro players have chosen to return to college for business reasons creates a convenient — but disingenuous — talking point. It's easy, and phony, to frame it as "pro players" returning to college. They're ALL pro players at this point, even if the NCAA and its members continue to covet an antitrust exemption that will allow them to restrict the amount of money the players can make, thereby diverting the finite booster funds toward the program, and the coaches. It's really that simple. The powers-that-be want to reduce the revenue stream for player, because that money can otherwise be funneled to the schools. But they won't admit that, because that makes it harder to get public (and in turn political) support. It's easier to frame it as "pro players playing in college sports." Again, they're all professionals. As they should be. For decades. a corrupt system kept the players from getting their fair share. Now that they are, the fat cats who control college sports want to ensure that the players will get less. So that they can get more. The fact that LSU isn't participating in the ruse makes them an obvious target of the folks who are trying to perpetuate it. At some point, LSU should just stand up and tell the SEC to GFY.

stories.title: Key takeaways from Washington Commanders win vs. Bengals in NFL Week 11
stories.summary: Here’s what we learned about the Commanders from this Week 11 clash with the Bengals after watching it live
stories.detailText: We all knew how important this game was. The Commanders beat the Giants in a season-saving Thursday night victory over the New York Giants. Then we waited a full 11 days to see the response. The entire NFC East won in that span, adding import to this intraconference clash with a Bengals team that was hot to trot. The Bengals receivers are so good. We all know that. The Commanders didn’t care. They came straight at Cincinnati in a super fun way. This was a game the Commanders needed, especially with the rest of the NFC East leading this week with a win. Could Washington maintain position within the division? We certainly found out. Jayden Daniels’ clutch play set up the win 🙌 pic.twitter.com/kmRDwepJ8v — NFL (@NFL) November 24, 2026 That gave the Commanders a 22-20 victory over the Cincinnati Bengals on Monday night. Let’s talk about the Commanders takeaways after watching this game live: Another close one The Commanders were dictated to early in the second half. That’s not a good thing. Washington was able to keep the points coming but not in the way you would like. With field goal after field goal, Washington was not able to keep up with a Bengals team that’s built on making you pay over time. That leads us to another close contest. The Commanders scored on four straight possessions yet were down one point at 17-16, and Washington just kept driving and driving and putting the Bengals in a bad spot. We found ourselves in a fourth-down spot where Drew Stevens hit a 41-yard attempt with 2 minutes 26 seconds left. Commanders take the lead with 2:26 remaining in the game 👀 CINvsWAS on ESPN Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/YEaVzDLKE9 — NFL (@NFL) November 24, 2026 That left the Bengals with a chance to go win it, as the two-minute waring passed. Then the Bengals made a play. Burrow connected with Mike Giesicki on a ball that put the Bengals in field-goal range. There was a Nick Cross sack that pushed the ball back to the point where the Bengals had to take a long field-goal try. The Bengals hit the field goal from 56 yards out. Daniels had less than a minute left and no timeouts to go. Daniels pushed the ball into midfield and then hit Antonio Williams for a 22 yard gain that set up a 26-yard field goal with four seconds left to win the game. Game, Hail Raisers. Lights come (off) Let’s examine what we learned about the Commanders after watching this game live: Northwest Stadium is the literal worst. As in, the wort stadium in the NFL. That became clear in the third quarter, when the lights went out. Like, for real. The Commanders found a way to keep the Bengals off balance and finally found some time of possession with good defense and some smart runs by Jayden Daniels. That tied the game at 10-10, leaving this game in the balance as we headed into the second half. OFF AND RUNNIN' 📺 #CINvsWAS ESPN pic.twitter.com/ADOfAwThMy — Washington Commanders (@Commanders) November 24, 2026 All in all, this was death by a thousand cuts. Just too many times the Commanders were beat for small gains (or losses) that wore this team down over time. The explosiveness that was expected didn’t percolate, which kept this game close as the game progressed. Commanders defense came to play There was so much talk about quarterback Joe Burrow and his efficiency, and for good reason. The Commanders made life so hard on the elite quarterback and the Bengals offense. It almost makes you want to see what coordinator Daronte Jones can do over a longer period. While the Bengals still managed to move the ball, Washington made life super difficult in the early going. big time stop 📺 #CINvsWAS ESPN pic.twitter.com/gntOtyZTCI — Washington Commanders (@Commanders) November 24, 2026 The Commanders offense didn’t help things out with real inefficiency that made yards to come by, but Jones came correct. The blitzes worked. The coverage plan worked. Washington’s offense needed to counter, which was not always the case. I think we can all admit the play calling was good. The offense’s inability to stay on the field was, well, not. I think we have something in Jones. Will the Commanders stick with him? We’ll freaking see, but it’s worth considering what Washington can be under this coordinator.

stories.title: Lighting error briefly leaves Commanders-Bengals ‘MNF’ game in dark as Roger Goodell looks on
stories.summary: A brief power outage at Northwest Stadium paused Monday night’s game between the Bengals and Commanders.
stories.detailText: Billy Joel once sang about seeing the lights go down on Broadway, and now football fans can say they saw the lights go down at Northwest Stadium. The “Monday Night Football” game between the Bengals and Commanders was briefly delayed after the lights went out in the middle of the third quarter just as Jayden Daniels was lining up to hike the ball on third-and-14. Stadium lights turn off during the third quarter between the Cincinnati Bengals and Washington Commanders at Northwest Stadium. IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The ESPN broadcast initially reported that the issue was “power-related and not the stadium” and later added that it had occurred due to “regularly scheduled maintenance for 10 p.m.” by the “lighting vendor” that was never disabled. “It’s a weekday thing, and they forgot it was a Monday night game,” ESPN broadcaster Joe Buck said on the broadcast. The lights in the stadium went out at the beginning of the third quarter of Bengals-Commanders. pic.twitter.com/f3yeTJONCt — ESPN (@espn) November 24, 2026 All the lights in the stadium went out at first, causing the refs to blow the whistle with 11:59 left in the third quarter. After several seconds, the electric signage that wraps around the stadium and the video board came back on, providing some light inside the Landover, Maryland venue. “Somebody turned out the lights,” Buck said. The telecast showed Bengals quarterback Joe Burrow throwing a football around to keep warm. NFL commissioner Roger Goodell was also on hand in the suit of Commanders owner Josh Harris. ESPN threw to commercials after several moments and when the network returned, the lights also returned. The Bengals were holding a 10-7 lead at the time of the power outage and when play resumed, Commanders quarterback Jayden Daniels was forced to throw the ball away. The Cincinnati Bengals and the Washington Commanders stand on the field after the lights went off during a game in Landover, Md., Monday, Nov. 23, 2026. Getty Images NFL commissioner Roger Goodell looks on as the lights go out during Commanders-Bengals. ESPN/X Washington settled for a field goal that briefly tied the game at 10-10. Monday’s incident is just the latest to occur at the outdated home of the Commanders. On Jan. 2, 2022, a railing broke at what was then known as FedEx Field sending several football fans tumbling in a near-tragic incident. Players look on after the lights go out during the third quarter of the game between the Cincinnati Bengals and Washington Commanders at Northwest Stadium. IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Raw sewage soaked fans in one section of the stadium during a game against the Chargers after a pipe burst on Sept. 12, 2021. The Commanders are building a new stadium at the site of the former RFK Stadium in Washington, D.C., that is scheduled to open in 2030. Speaking with ESPN ahead of the game, Goodell expressed excitement over the new stadium. “I’m a kid who grew up here. And so I remember going to RFK Stadium. And I think the work that they’ve done just on the architectural side of it and the construction of it, I think it’s going to be remarkable,” the NFL commissioner said, according to Front Office Sports ..” And having it on the same site, I think it’s going to have a wonderful emotional connection. Being in the District is special. And I just think that’s going to be a wonderful moment, not only for the league but for the fans.”

stories.title: Monday Night Football: Joe Burrow's second TD pass puts Bengals up 17-10
stories.summary: The lights are back on and both offenses have put up points in the third quarter.
stories.detailText: Bengals quarterback Joe Burrow has been throwing touchdown passes in bunches recently and he's up to two in Washington on Monday night. Burrow found rookie wideout Colbie Young for a 4-yard touchdown while rolling to his right and the Bengals are now up 17-10 on the Commanders with 7:04 to play in the third quarter. stories.title: Sources: Packers' Micah Parsons cleared to make season debut Wednesday vs. Rams
stories.summary: Packers star Micah Parsons has been cleared and is set for his season debut against the Rams on Wednesday night, sources told NFL Network's Ian Rapoport.
stories.detailText: GREEN BAY, Wis. -- Welcome back, Micah Parsons . The Green Bay Packers ' star pass rusher was cleared Monday to return from last season's knee injury and is expected to make his 2026 debut Wednesday night against the Los Angeles Rams , sources told NFL Network's Ian Rapoport. Earlier Monday, Parsons said he still needed final clearance from Dr. Neal ElAttrache, who performed the surgery. Parsons, who injured his left knee in Week 15 last season, still needs to be officially activated off the physically unable to perform list. That move did not happen before the end of NFL business Monday. Parsons' return to game action will come 347 days after he not only tore his ACL but also his meniscus in a noncontact injury against the Denver Broncos . Parsons first returned to practice Nov. 4 and did only individual drills that week. The following week, he began to incorporate team (11-on-11) drills into his work. The Packers then had their bye following the Nov. 15 loss to the Minnesota Vikings , but it was not a full bye week because of the Thanksgiving Eve game. The Packers resumed practice Saturday and practiced for three days before they depart for Los Angeles on Tuesday. "I would say I feel like I've done everything I possibly could to put myself in position to potentially play on Wednesday but for sure this season," Parsons said Monday. "And I'll be looking forward to returning to the field." Parsons is expected to be on a snap count upon his return. Despite having a winning record (6-4), the Packers sit in last place in the NFC North, where the Chicago Bears , Detroit Lions and Vikings are all 7-2. "I'm so locked in on what's ahead of me and I understand what this game Wednesday means to the organization and I myself and what it means for playoffs," Parsons said. "And if I can be out there, I want to be out there and I'm excited for any time. Because we only got seven more games left, so I want to capitalize on all those if I can." Parsons led the Packers with 12.5 sacks last season and led the entire league with 64 pressures, according to ESPN Analytics, despite playing in only 14 games. It was his first season in Green Bay after the Packers gave up two first-round picks plus defensive tackle Kenny Clark to acquire Parsons from the Dallas Cowboys just days before the start of last season. But the Packers did not win a game after Parsons was injured last season. They were 9-3-1 heading into the Broncos game but lost five in a row, including an NFC wild-card playoff game against the Bears, to close the season. Without Parsons, the Packers have gone 6-9. "The only thing I'm targeting in a sense of mindset is to win every week to try to uplift this season, change this season around and do exactly what the Packers brought me here to do," Parsons said. "That's it. That's my only target and that's to make a run for the playoffs and make guys around me better. That's it." "So I have no targets and outcomes," Parsons added. "I think I've achieved everything that I've wanted in my career except for the big one and I think that's kind of like my own mindset and through the [Nick] Saban documentary I learned just stay in the process of every day. Own my process my today, so I owned it today. I got another process tomorrow and, God willing, I'll have another process Wednesday night and that'll be the start of this new journey."

stories.title: Monday Night Football: Bengals lead 10-7 at halftime
stories.summary: Both offenses took some time to get going on a rainy night in Washington.
stories.detailText: It took more than a quarter and a half for any points to get scored in Washington on Monday night, but the Bengals and Commanders finally got going in the final minutes before halftime. After a 15-play drive resulted in a field goal midway through the second quarter, the Bengals found more explosive plays on their next possession. Running back Samaje Perine broke free on a short pass for a 44-yard gain and Joe Burrow then went deep to wide receiver Tee Higgins for a 31-yard touchdown on the first play after the two-minute warning. The catch bore some resemblance to the one by Jaguars wideout Parker Washington that was ruled incomplete on Sunday, but there was no review. That score put the Bengals up 10-0 and left the Commanders with a last chance to find their first points of the evening. Jayden Daniels ran for one first down and threw for two more before hooking up with tight end Chig Okonkwo for a 32-yard gain that moved the Commanders to Cincinnati's 6-yard-line. A pass to wide receiver Treylon Burks in the end zone drew a pass interference flag on cornerback Dax Hill and running back Jacory Croskey-Merritt punched the ball in on the next play to make it 10-7 going into the break. Daniels is 8-of-11 for 85 yards, but has been sacked three times by Boye Mafe. The last of those came on a third down and led to an animated Stefon Diggs appearing to yell about throwing the ball on the sideline while the Bengals had possession. Diggs's only catch of the half came on the late touchdown drive. Burrow is 16-of-23 for 179 yards and has been sacked a couple of times. The Bengals also saw safety Bryan Cook leave just before halftime with an ankle injury and he's called questionable to be back on the field when the Commanders get the ball to start the second half.

stories.title: Sean McVay on Puka Nacua's future with Rams: 'Can't say for certain anything'
stories.summary: Sean McVay believes Rams star Puka Nacua will remain with the team, but he also knows the Rams will have other free agents they'll need to sign.
stories.detailText: Rams wide receiver Puka Nacua dives to catch a pass against the Washington Commanders on Nov. 8. (Nick Wass / Associated Press) Puka Nacua is done for the season, and while the Rams’ star receiver is a cornerstone of coach Sean McVay’s offense, his future with the franchise is not necessarily a done deal. Nacua, who had knee surgery last week, is in the final year of his rookie contract. If he had not been involved in a series of off-the-field incidents dating to 2025 , Nacua probably would have had a massive contract extension in hand before this season began. Instead, the 2025 NFL receptions leader is on track to become a free agent unless he and the Rams agree to an extension, or the Rams place the franchise tag on him or they trade him. Nacua, a 2023 fifth-round draft pick out of Brigham Young, is earning $5.8 million this season, according to Overthecap.com . He is one of several players who are eligible to become free agents, including defensive lineman Kobie Turner, edge rusher Byron Young and offensive linemen Kevin Dotson, Steve Avila and Warren McClendon Jr., among others. McVay was asked Monday if he expects Nacua to be with the Rams next season. “Yeah, we have a lot of guys that are free agents,” said McVay, who is preparing his team for Wednesday night’s game against the Green Bay Packers. ”What I’ve tried to really do is focus on right here, right now. “He’s obviously a guy that is a very important piece for us for now and for the future, but there are a lot of guys that fall under that category.” Can McVay say for certain that Nacua will be with the Rams in 2027? “I can’t say for certain anything,” McVay said. “Here’s what I’m not interested in, is something being taken out of context. ... When you go through the amount of free agents that we have, Puka is a huge part of the conversation that you love, but there are also guys that are part of his draft class… Read more: Plaschke: Without Puka Nacua, the Rams are done “There are mechanics that we’d like to be able to try to figure out how to keep these really good players and people that we love, and certainly Puka is at the forefront of our mind.” Nacua, 25, is the defendant in a civil lawsuit brought by a woman who alleges he made an antisemitic comment during a New Year’s Eve dinner and later bit her while riding in a vehicle. In March, Nacua checked himself into a rehab facility, and in a September interview with Netflix acknowledged alcohol use. Nacua sat out two games because of a hip injury and played through a calf injury before suffering knee and toe injuries in a Nov. 8 victory over the Washington Commanders . He was placed on injured reserve, had surgery Wednesday , and on Thursday the NFL suspended him three games for violating the league’s personal-conduct policy. “I think he’s growing and I trust his heart,” McVay said. “I think he’s making a lot of steps that are in the right direction.” Get the best, most interesting and strangest stories of the day from the L.A. sports scene and beyond from our newsletter The Sports Report. stories.title: David Bailey already drawing Hall of Fame comparison 10 games into Jets career
stories.summary: Davis said Bailey has only scratched the surface of what he can do.
stories.detailText: Jets linebacker David Bailey rehabs during practice in Florham Park, N.J., Thursday, Oct. 29, 2026. Demario Davis is in his 15th NFL season, and he has played with some greats. The Jets linebacker sees traits in rookie edge rusher David Bailey that he has observed in some of those great ones. Davis praised Bailey’s “process” on Monday, saying the rookie does not let outside factors affect his preparation routine, similarly to the best players he has been around. “I don’t know what all goes into his process, but I know I see him in the same spots around the building all the time,” Davis said. “That type of stuff is what I’ve seen from guys who are now in the Hall of Fame. When you come in and you go through the week, you see them in the same spots in the building all the time, whether it was an All-Pro wide receiver or an All-Pro running back or an All-Pro quarterback, an All-Pro defensive end in Cam Jordan — a solidified Hall of Famer, one of the best I’ve ever seen do it — it’s all about that process. Those guys have a regimen and a routine that doesn’t change based on what’s going on around them. That’s very rare to see for a rookie.” Jets linebacker David Bailey rehabs during practice in Florham Park, N.J., Thursday, Oct. 29, 2026. Bill Kostroun for NY Post Bailey has been a star on the field. He added two sacks against the Chargers to bring his season total to 9 ½, just shy of Hugh Douglas’ Jets rookie record of 10 set in 1995. He is five away from Jevon Kearse’s NFL rookie record of 14 ½, established in 1999. Davis said Bailey has only scratched the surface of what he can do. “He’s only going to get better,” the veteran linebacker said. “It’s going to be scary for a lot of quarterbacks for a long time and it’s going to be good for the Jets for a long time.” The Jets gave up a touchdown just before halftime Sunday when Chargers quarterback Justin Herbert ran for a 10-yard score as time expired. The Jets showed an interesting defense on the play, with three players rushing and eight players lined up on the goal line. Herbert took off, and the Jets could not bring him down. If they had tackled him, the Chargers might have been unable to even kick a field goal. Both Dane Belton and Davis missed tackles on the play. “They had a chance to try to score on a throwing play and we had guys in the end zone,” head coach Aaron Glenn said, “but then again, if he had a chance to run it, we had guys able to converge on the ball and I think if you look at that play, I think we had two missed tackles, which would’ve put them in a tough situation with six seconds to try to run the ball in that situation. The thing is we just got to make that tackle. We make that tackle; we put ourselves in a good position.”

stories.title: Seahawks to monitor Sam Darnold status this week before final call vs. 49ers
stories.summary: The Seahawks still plan to start Sam Darnold against the 49ers but will wait to see how the QB looks in practice Wednesday before making a final call.
stories.detailText: RENTON, Wash. -- The Seattle Seahawks still plan to start Sam Darnold against the San Francisco 49ers on Sunday but will wait to see how the quarterback looks in practice Wednesday before making a final decision, coach Mike Macdonald said. Darnold has missed the past two games because of a quad injury he suffered near the end of Seattle's loss to the Chicago Bears in Week 8, when he also suffered a cracked rib on his first dropback of the night. Macdonald said last Monday that Darnold would start this week as long as he made the progress over the bye that the team was projecting. Speaking with reporters Monday, Macdonald said the quarterback made "a good bit of progress." "He was able to train a little bit here, do some rehab here," Macdonald said. "He also was able to get away. He's optimistic, but I think just with today's practice cadence and speed today, I think it's probably wise to wait to make any declarations until we get through Wednesday's practice." The Seahawks held a bonus practice Monday coming off their bye. They were not required to release an injury report, but Darnold -- who had not practiced since the Nov. 2 Bears game -- was seen jogging out for warmups with his helmet on, and Macdonald confirmed that he took part. "He looked great," the coach said. "Everything was positive today. He took a ton of reps, but it wasn't a full-speed -- it was more of a [walk-through] tempo." With the first-place 49ers (9-1) winning Sunday night, the reigning Super Bowl champion Seahawks (6-4) are now three games back in the NFC West standings heading into Sunday's game at Levi's Stadium. San Francisco won the first meeting at Lumen Field in October. Darnold's quad and rib injuries were the latest setbacks in what has been a trying start to the season. He injured his glute on the fifth play of the opener, missing the remainder of that game and the following week. In six full games, he has thrown 10 touchdown passes and nine interceptions. Backup Drew Lock , meanwhile, has thrown seven touchdown passes with zero interceptions over the four games in which he has filled in -- all Seattle victories. Lock has been dealing with a right elbow injury for over a month, and he also played through an oblique injury last week while quarterbacking Seattle to a win over the Las Vegas Raiders . "I'd say the bye week was really helpful for Drew," Macdonald said. "I think a well-deserved chance for him to feel better, and that's going to help us moving forward. But I think that's the case for several of our guys as well." Macdonald did not have injury updates on any other players Monday. Defensive tackle Leonard Williams missed the past two games with a stinger that kept him out of practice both weeks. He was on the field for warmups Monday with his helmet. Players not seen during the warmup period Monday included right tackle Abe Lucas , right guard Anthony Bradford and left guard Quenton Nelson . Lucas left the Raiders game and did not return after suffering an ankle sprain. Nelson, acquired in an Oct. 27 trade with the Indianapolis Colts , is recovering from a knee procedure that kept him out of the past two games. Bradford has started in Nelson's absence, but he has been dealing with a knee injury. "With the injuries right now, it's tough to make declarations," Macdonald said. "So I'd say we haven't ruled anybody out yet, nor anybody in. So we'll wait until Wednesday really to give you a firm update on probably all the folks that you're curious about. Some guys it's pretty clear, some guys it's not so clear, so I think it's better to wait a couple days until we're clear on everything." Seattle on Monday placed George Holani on injured reserve after the backup running back suffered a knee injury against the Raiders. Madcdonald said he did not know if Holani would need surgery. The Seahawks also promoted cornerback Trevon Diggs and tackle Bobby Hart from their practice squad to their 53-man roster.

stories.title: J.J. McCarthy knows he can be better despite being more than enough for Giants so far
stories.summary: McCarthy has averaged 211.2 passing yards and 22.5 rushing yards in four starts, with two touchdowns, one interception and a 60.3 completion percentage.
stories.detailText: J.J. McCarthy sailed passes long and wide. He missed open receivers by several yards. He struggled with pressure, bungling multiple opportunities to put away the Jaguars, who dared the 23-year-old to burn their Cover Zero defense. When Jacksonville head coach Liam Coen curiously opted to kick a 26-yard field goal to cut its deficit to five with less than four minutes remaining, he was banking on the Giants being unable to pick up a first down for the fifth straight drive.
