We can’t give them that confidence. … The next time we get in those situations where we’re up, we have to finish the job. “As an offense, we’re going to do everything we can to make sure we close that one out a little bit earlier. Starting with myself, there’s a lot of throws I want to get back.” McCarthy went 0-for-9 on throws of at least 20 yards. He had a stretch of nine straight incompletions, as the Giants managed only three second-half points. But at the end of his most erratic game with the Giants, McCarthy (18-of-38, 173 passing yards, with one touchdown, no interceptions) stood in the pocket with a pass-rusher bearing down on him and delivered a 19-yard pass to Malachi Fields between multiple defenders, helping seal the team’s biggest win of the season. Fans greet Giants quarterback J.J. McCarthy (18) as he walks off the field after a game at MetLife Stadium on Sunday, Nov. 22, 2026. Corey Sipkin for NY Post “He threaded that needle right past that linebacker. That was a big-time throw,” head coach John Harbaugh said. “That’s a confident guy, and he’s been in a lot of huge games. And we’re going to start hitting some of those deep passes. We wanted to take some shots. We wanted to go after them downfield, and we did, and those are going to start happening. We’ll start making those plays for sure.” Despite McCarthy’s uneven effort, the Giants (6-3-1) improved to 3-1 with the third-year quarterback as the starter. New York Giants quarterback J.J. McCarthy (18) throws a pass during the first half against an opponent in Brooklyn, N.Y., Sunday, Nov. 22, 2026. Corey Sipkin for NY Post Since debuting with 243 passing yards, one touchdown and one interception in the fourth quarter of the loss to the Saints. McCarthy has averaged 211.2 passing yards and 22.5 rushing yards in four starts, with two touchdowns, one interception and a 60.3 completion percentage. McCarthy may never resemble the top 10 draft pick the Vikings expected to become the face of their franchise, but the former Michigan star — who was acquired two months ago for a 2027 fifth-round pick — has kept the Giants afloat without Jaxson Dart by riding a dominant defense and largely avoiding devastating mistakes — a formula the Wolverines used to win a national championship with McCarthy in 2023. “J.J. [came] in mid-season, but you just can tell by his leadership how much he wants to win, how much he’s a competitor and how many people that he brings around with him,” said Malik Nabers, who caught his first touchdown from McCarthy on Sunday. In the first half, McCarthy led the Giants to 20 points against the league’s No. 2 scoring defense. The quarterback, who was the team’s leading rusher before going into victory formation, put the Giants in position to blow the game open late in the third quarter — leading by 14 and driving in Jacksonville territory — before Cam Skattebo fumbled and Jaguars safety Antonio Johnson ran the other way with the ball. McCarthy then made perhaps the day’s most important play, sprinting across the field to bring down Johnson , preventing a defensive touchdown that could have swung the game. “In a weird way, I look forward to those moments to put some contact out there and make a tackle,” McCarthy said. “At the end of the day, you have to do your job as a quarterback. When everything goes wrong, try to find a way to make it right.”

stories.title: Making sense of Liam Coen's nonsensical decision to kick a late field goal
stories.summary: Jacksonville's loss to the Giants on Sunday included a nonsensical decision with 3:43 to play.
stories.detailText: {"unknownError":"There has been an error","expiredError":"This video has been expired due to copyright restrictions.","unavailableError":"This content is not yet available.","georestrictedError":"This content is not available in your location.","networkId":"169843","adManagerUrl":"https://mssl.fwmrm.net/libs/adm/6.51.0/AdManager.js","serverId":"https://29773.v.fwmrm.net/ad/g/1","profileId":"169843:nbcu_web_jwp_cs_moat_https","afid":"140315314","caid":"nbcs_nbc_pft_liam_coens_261123","csid":"nbcsports_embed_on_domain","sfid":"","adHocGroup":"","athlete":"","businessUnit":"NBC Sports","category":"","duration":"320120","event":"","externalAdvertiserId":"nbcs_nbc_pft_liam_coens_261123","genre":"News","guid":"nbc_pft_liam_coens_261123","league":"NFL","network":"","platform":"PC","playlist":"","show":"ProFootballTalk","sport":"Football","subtype":"","team":"Jacksonville Jaguars, New York Giants","title": "Coen lacked confidence in 4th against Giants","datePublished":"","videoPageUrl": "https://www.nbcsports.com/watch/nfl/profootballtalk/jaguars-liam-coen-lacked-confidence-in-4th-quarter-against-new-york-giants","availableDate":"2026-11-23T14:00:00Z","expirationDate":"","countries":""} Jacksonville's loss to the Giants on Sunday included a nonsensical decision with 3:43 to play. Down by eight points and facing fourth and goal from the New York eight, Jaguars coach Liam Coen decided to kick a field goal. After the game, Jaguars coach Liam Coen justified the decision to take the three points by calling an effort to score a touchdown a " hope play ." We hope he's not serious. It was eight yards, not 80. Regardless of what the analytics said, it was time to go for the touchdown, which with a successful two-point conversion would have tied the game. As explained on Monday's PFT Live , I think the two-point conversion was the deciding factor for Coen. When the score was 23-9, the Jaguars scored a touchdown that cut the margin to eight. After the touchdown, Coen played the all-too-common analytics game, opting to go for two in the hopes of cutting the margin to six and ideally avoiding overtime if they had scored again. When it was time to go for two, Coen utilized his best two-point play based on the specific matchup of the Jacksonville offense against the New York defense. It failed. Which meant that, if/when the Jaguars scored another touchdown, they would need to rely on Coen's second-best two-point play. After Plan A failed, why would Coen believe Plan B would succeed? And so instead of going for a touchdown which may or may not have been capped by a successful two-point try, Coen opted to take the three and kick off. Which pissed off the New York offense , and which helped set the stage for the Jaguars never getting the ball again. If the Jaguars had gone for the score, the Giants would have gotten the ball deep in their own end. The Jaguars would have been likely to get another shot at a touchdown and a two-point conversion. Still, the Jaguars would have had to convert a two-point play after their best option at going for two had failed. In the moment, that reality may have been the difference for Coen. Which brings us back to the analytics-driven trend to go for two after scoring a touchdown when trailing by 14. If the two-pointer fails, the coach needs to be confident in the second-best two-point play for the week. Coen likely wasn't, which contributed to the decision to not try to gain eight yards in a one-score game. That's the most important factor when it comes to relying on math. Once teams start down the go-for-two path, their confidence (or lack thereof) in the potential for successful two-point plays becomes critical. Coen's best two-point play failed. Which may have shaken his faith in his second-best two-point play. Which may have prompted him to opt for the three points in lieu of rolling the dice on scoring from the eight — before rolling the dice on scoring again from the two.

stories.title: Christian McCaffrey puts 49ers’ loss of ‘true warrior’ in perspective
stories.summary: Christian McCaffrey had the closest view of anyone on the 49ers roster when Colton McKivitz suffered a gruesome injury that ended his season during Sunday night’s 35-10 victory against the...
stories.detailText: Christian McCaffrey had the closest view of anyone on the 49ers roster when Colton McKivitz suffered a gruesome injury that ended his season during Sunday night’s 35-10 victory against the Vikings in Mexico City. On Monday, McCaffrey posted a photo of himself consoling the 49ers’ right tackle on his Instagram story, sharing his gratitude. 49ers Colton McKivitz seen carted off the field in Sunday’s game against the Vikings. AFP via Getty Images “A true warrior. A staple of this team. Love you brother @cmckivitz53,” McCaffrey captioned the photo of him hugging McKivitz after the injury occurred. McKivitz was seen landing on top of McCaffrey in an awkward position on the play that derailed his season. On Monday, the 49ers announced that he suffered a fractured and dislocated left ankle on the play. Christian McCaffrey posted a message on his IG story for Colton McKivitz after his devastating season ending injury pic.twitter.com/PXIthV9ksa — OurSF49ers (@OurSf49ers) November 24, 2026 San Francisco 49ers running back Christian McCaffrey rushing down the field during Sunday’s game against the Vikings. Getty Images McCaffrey was one of the many 49ers players who were seen left devastated following the play, as left tackle Trent Williams was seen slamming his helmet on the ground after the injury happened. Before McKivitz was carted off the field, McCaffrey was one of the last 49ers players to talk to him, and that’s when the 49ers running back was consoling the offensive lineman. 49ers’ offensive lineman Colton McKivitz was carted off the field during Sunday’s game against the Vikings. AP Photo/Eduardo Verdugo When the game ended, McCaffrey told reporters “[He’s one of the heart and souls of this team. He is the standard and we’re gonna miss him. We all love him, and we’re praying for him,” McCaffrey told reporters following the game. “It’s one of the worst parts of this game, is stuff like that.” McKivitz is in his seventh year in the NFL and has turned into a franchise right tackle after the 49ers selected him in the fifth round of the 2020 NFL Draft. This season, he’s played a vital part in the success of McCaffrey, and quarterback Brock Purdy has been among the fewest-sacked starting quarterbacks this year. McCaffrey has run the ball 127 times through 10 games this season and is averaging 4.5 yards per rush with 11 touchdowns.

stories.title: The Fearsome Foursome set the standard. Can the Rams’ new front four live up to it?
stories.summary: Aaron Donald, Myles Garrett and the Rams' star-studded defensive line are finally healthy as Los Angeles honors the legendary Fearsome Foursome against the Packers.
stories.detailText: The Los Angeles Rams are bringing back the Fearsome Foursome on Wednesday night. Not the one that terrorized NFL quarterbacks in the 1960s . That group belongs in football immortality. This one has Aaron Donald, Myles Garrett, Kobie Turner, and Byron Young. Four defensive linemen with enough talent to make opposing quarterbacks think twice about hanging on to the football. There’s just been one problem. They haven’t all been healthy enough to wreak havoc together. Until now. Byron Young (left), Kobie Turner (left-middle), Braden Fiske (right-middle) and Myles Garrett (right) wearing the Rams’ inaugural “Fearsome White” jerseys that will be unveiled during the Thanksgiving Eve game between the Green Bay Packers and Los Angeles Rams on Netflix (Credit: Los Angeles Rams) With Turner returning from a groin injury and Garrett finally finding his footing after knee surgery, the Rams could have their entire defensive front available for the first time this season when they host the Green Bay Packers on Thanksgiving Eve. And the timing couldn’t be more appropriate. The Rams will unveil their Fearsome White alternate uniforms Wednesday, paying tribute to the legendary defensive line of Deacon Jones, Merlin Olsen, Rosey Grier and Lamar Lundy. Grier will be honored on the field alongside family members of the original Fearsome Foursome, while the Rams will wear throwback-inspired uniforms celebrating the franchise’s defensive dominance of the 1960s. But the current group doesn’t want to spend the evening playing dress-up. They want to make some history of their own. “When we go out there and play to the best of our ability, and we rush four as one, five as one, we’re a very, very scary unit,” Turner said Monday. “I don’t want to put too much out there up front. I want our work to be able to show itself, and I think it’s going to show itself on Wednesday.” The Los Angeles Rams defensive front four, Lamar Lundy, left, Merlin Olsen, Rosey Grier, and Deacon Jones, pose in a 1964 photo. AP That’s a fairly bold statement from a player who hasn’t shared the field with the Rams’ complete collection of pass rushers this season. Donald is a three-time NFL Defensive Player of the Year. Garrett is the reigning champ and has won the award twice. Young has developed into a dangerous edge rusher, while Turner provides the kind of interior disruption that can collapse a pocket before a quarterback finishes his drop. Before the season, this group looked like a dream for defensive coordinator Chris Shula. But on the field, it has largely remained an unfinished experiment. Los Angeles Rams defensive tackle Aaron Donald (99) greets defensive end Myles Garrett (95) during an NFL game in Landover, Md., Sunday, Nov. 8, 2026. AP Photo/Stephanie Scarbrough Garrett understands the history he’s being asked to honor. The Rams linebacker revealed Monday that he studied Jones while growing up, watching footage of the Hall of Fame pass rusher who helped popularize the quarterback sack as an official measure of defensive dominance. “I was watching Deacon Jones in high school, watching ‘Top 100,’ listening to him speak, him coining the term ‘sack,’ how much he’s done for this game,” Garrett said. But Garrett’s admiration apparently went beyond watching old highlights. Asked whether he ever tried Jones’ infamous head slap, a technique that was eventually outlawed by the NFL, Garrett couldn’t help laughing. “In high school I did, for sure,” Garrett admitted. “I got away with it for a little while too.” Somewhere, Jones would probably appreciate that confession. Donald, meanwhile, said he has spent his Rams career trying to uphold the standard established by the franchise’s original defensive giants. “Coming here as a rookie, you heard about it,” Donald said. “I always try to live up to their success and everything they were able to do.” The challenge Wednesday isn’t simply honoring history. It’s stopping a Green Bay offense capable of turning a broken play into a 50-yard touchdown. Packers quarterback Jordan Love has developed a dangerous connection with his deep threats, including Christian Watson and Matthew Golden. But throwing deep requires time, and that’s precisely what the Rams hope to take away. “They’re going to take their shots. They’re going to test our back end,” Turner said. “But for them to even have that opportunity, they have to hold the ball a little bit longer. And that’s where this defensive front comes into play.” Braden Fiske, Kobie Turner and Byron Young of the Los Angeles Rams celebrate a sack during a game against the New Orleans Saints in Inglewood, Calif., Nov. 2, 2025. Getty Images Defensive coordinator Chris Shula has resisted comparisons between his current group and the original Fearsome Foursome, preferring to emphasize chemistry, preparation and getting his best players healthy. It should be pointed out that the original four earned their reputation over years of dominance, not one nationally televised game. But there’s something fitting about the Rams finally unleashing their complete defensive front on a night dedicated to the men who helped redefine the position. “It’s our job to go out there on Wednesday night in front of the entire world and show that legacy, and make sure that they’re proud,” Turner said. The Rams will provide the white uniforms, the vintage graphics and the historical tribute. The rest is up to Donald, Garrett and company. After all, the best way to honor the Fearsome Foursome isn’t by looking like them. It’s by making Jordan Love feel what opposing quarterbacks felt 60 years ago. stories.title: ESPN continues Tom Jackson tributes during 'Monday Night Football'
stories.summary: Tributes for Tom Jackson, the former ESPN NFL analyst who died Friday at the age of 75, continued as the Bengals faced the Commanders.
stories.detailText: The tributes for Tom Jackson continued as ESPN aired the Nov. 23 edition of "Monday Night Football" between the Cincinnati Bengals and Washington Commanders . As play-by-play announcer Joe Buck opened the broadcast , the "NFL Primetime" music played in the background. Jackson, the former ESPN NFL studio analyst who co-hosted the weekly Sunday highlight show alongside Chris Berman for nearly three decades, died Friday at the age of 75. No cause of death has been provided. "He was a wonderful being first and foremost," ESPN color commentator Troy Aikman said during the pregame show. As a player, Aikman said, Jackson and Berman were must-see television – both in an entertainment sense but also because that was how fans saw what happened around the league that week. "They were so good," Aikman said. The former Dallas Cowboys quarterback respected that they could be critical and opinionated without attacking the individual. "I could throw three interceptions in a game, and we could lose, and I could watch Primetime and not wanna go hang myself at the end of the night," Aikman said. "They just had a respectful way of presenting the information and letting everybody know what happened, but doing it the right way, I thought." Troy Aikman: "I could throw three interceptions in a game, and we could lose, and I could watch [NFL Primetime] and not want to go hang myself at the end of the night. They had a respectful way of presenting the information and letting everybody know what happened..." pic.twitter.com/Fu3f0aiMpp — Awful Announcing (@awfulannouncing) November 24, 2026 During the beginning of the second quarter, Buck welcomed viewers over the “Primetime” theme once again. “There are a lot of heavy hearts in our company as the NFL and ESPN family has lost a legend this past week,” Buck said. Aikman repeated his stance that “Primetime” was “must-watch” every Sunday. “He was obviously a big part of the football season for many years,” Aikman said. Joe Buck and Troy Aikman remember ESPN legend Tom Jackson during MNF ♥️ pic.twitter.com/nvIkrcDz8x — ESPN (@espn) November 24, 2026 Berman announced Jackson's death Nov. 22 during "Sunday NFL Countdown." To honor the former Denver Broncos linebacker who was part of the vaunted "Orange Crush" defense, the ESPN crew sported orange ties throughout the show. ESPN also released a five-minute video of Jackson surprising Berman at the studio just a few weeks before his unexpected passing. During halftime of Monday night's game, Berman hosted a special edition of his "Fastest 3 Minutes" segment solo. After once again eulogizing his best friend on air, Berman did the highlights of the Broncos' 38-24 victory over the Las Vegas Raiders on Sunday. Then in typical "Boomer" and "Teej" fashion, the package shifted to highlights of Denver's 1977 AFC championship game victory, including postgame locker-room footage of Jackson, over the Raiders. The best “fastest three minutes” you’ll ever see. Thank you Boomer and @ESPNNFL for your incredible tribute to everyone’s best friend, TJ. 🧡 pic.twitter.com/pTHGCpAlJM — Denver Broncos (@Broncos) November 24, 2026 A special "TJ" logo with his Jackson's jersey number, 57, appeared in the upper right hand corner of the screen throughout halftime. teamStories.detailText: DENVER, CO - NOVEMBER 22: Denver Broncos running back Jonah Coleman (20) celebrates with guard Quinn Meinerz (77) in the end zone with his third quarter touchdown against the Las Vegas Raiders at Empower Field at Mile High on November 22, 2026 in Denver, Colorado. (Photo by Dustin Bradford/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The Denver Broncos found one thing against the Las Vegas Raiders on Sunday that they haven’t had since early last year. A potent rushing attack. Sure they had more total rushing yards against the Arizona Cardinals, but that was due to Bo Nix having that 60+ yard rush. Nix had 6 carries for 5 yards on Sunday. No, this 133 yard rushing total was behind the legs of Jonah Coleman and a revitalized offensive line. When asked about the line’s improvement, head coach Sean Payton was quite pleased overall. “If the offensive line improved, then you’re going to run the ball better,” Payton said on Monday. |So I think you’re asking was the offensive line improved or better. I think we played really good in the front. Obviously we played more players. I thought from a protection standpoint and from a run game standpoint, there were a lot of good things to be excited about.” That last part is the most interesting. If Payton saw a lot of good things to be excited about, then we should also feel a lot better about where they might be heading into the part of the year when a strong rushing attack is how you win games in the NFL. Broncos daily recap Ja’Quan McMillian is the best ballhawking cornerback in Denver since Aqib Talib The Denver Broncos have to find a way to extend the best ballhawking cornerback in the orange and blue since Aqib Talib. Broncos Stock Up, Stock Down: Week 11 vs. Raiders The Broncos offense exploded for 31 points vs. the Las Vegas Raiders, led by the arm of quarterback Bo Nix and the 100-yard, 3-touchdown performance by rookie running back Jonah Coleman. Despite that, the Raiders still had a shot to tie it up late in the game, but that man we all want paid, cornerback Ja’Quan McMillian, said nah nah, and called the game with a game-sealing pick-six of rookie quarterback Fernando Mendoza. 7 things we learned from the Broncos 38-24 win over the Raiders The Broncos beat the Raiders on Sunday to increase their winning streak to six games and put them in the AFC West lead. Game balls for the Broncos’ win over Raiders in Week 11 The Denver Broncos let the Las Vegas Raiders back in it, but then closed it out convincingly to move to 8-2. Here are who we give our game balls to for the win. The Bills, Chiefs, and Jaguars: The Broncos race for AFC dominance With Denver’s win over the Las Vegas Raiders on Sunday, the Broncos again find themselves atop the AFC West and the 2nd seed in the AFC. As Denver looks around the NFL at their closest competition, it’s clear that with just 7-weeks to go in the regular season that their main concerns are the Bills, Chiefs, and Jaguars. Potent quotables Sean Payton On what has contributed to the offense’s jump in success over the last four weeks “In fairness, it’s hard to look at one specific thing. Certainly when you look at the early start of the season, we played some really, really good defenses. That’d be a starting point. Then secondly, hopefully we’re improving in some of the areas we discussed, red zone, third down, et cetera. I think it’s hard to just say one thing.” On RB Jonah Coleman’s heavy workload against the Raiders leading into a short week “We have a program relative to a Thursday game, relative to a Friday game. Certainly when a runner has the snaps or pitch count he had yesterday, we’ll take all of that into account. The recovery today will be important, tomorrow the same way. Obviously we feel like it’s a position [where] we have really good depth. He got going yesterday. [RB] J.K. [Dobbins] is healthy, and who our third back is, we have some flexibility. So I think we really look at the schedule of recovery with a Friday game. It’s been a minute since I can recall it. There’s always one of these itineraries that’s new. So heading east for a Friday game, what’s that look like? Just from experience, we’ll put that itinerary together.” On what stood out about QB Bo Nix’s downfield passing against the Raiders and how run game success created those opportunities “You guys have heard it before. When you’re running the ball well or you’re maybe getting a defense into a little bit more down safety look, there are some routes that you like that maybe aren’t as attractive when they’re holding their shells. So it kind of goes hand in hand, especially the play-action.” On the defensive performance against the Raiders “Generally speaking if you’re looking at it, there were three or four explosives or big plays, if you will. There was an MA (missed assignment) in one. We had an injury prior to another one, but things that we’ll have to clean up today with film study and be better at as we move forward.” On what DL Zach Allen does best “Great question. He’s an exceptional athlete. I think the other thing is he has real good football instincts. So he is quick. He can feel a quarterback throwing and get a tipped ball. There are a lot of things I don’t want to say come natural to him, but his football instincts along with his staying power and his athleticism I think give you what we’re able to see now.” On the process of deciding to stick with a running back when he gets rolling “The trickiest thing is the first half kind of went quick, and we were in a two-minute drill. [RB] J.K. [Dobbins] is going to be super important for what we’re doing in this stretch. Obviously [RB] Jonah [Coleman]. Then we feel like there are some backs that’ll be coming back off of injury, whether it’s [RB] RJ [Harvey], [RB] Tyler [Badie]. teamStories.detailText: (Photo by Manuel Velasquez/Getty Images) | Getty Images Week 11 saw the Las Vegas Raiders continue to struggle against the playoff contenders on their schedule, falling 38-24 to the Denver Broncos on Sunday . But let’s check in on a few old friends and see how the weekend went for a few former Raiders: Kirk Cousins, Tre’von Moehrig and Marcus Epps. Kirk Cousins Score: 35-10 Vikings lose Stats: 26/38 (68.4%), 235 yards, 0 TDs, 1 INT Cousins’ last start with the Raiders was a 38-17 loss to the San Francisco 49ers, and his second start with the Minnesota Vikings this season was a 35-10 loss to the 49ers. Clearly, San Francisco just has his number, as facing the same team/defense twice in three weeks didn’t make a difference the second time around. There’s no shame in that since San Francisco looks like a Super Bowl favorite, asserting its dominance over another contender for the top seed in the NFC. Tre’von Moehrig Score: 35-33 Panthers win Stats: 6 tackles Considering how bad the Baltimore Ravens have been without Lamar Jackson, this game was way too close for the Carolina Panthers. But the Panthers managed to get a big win that gives them a two-game lead in the NFC South. Moehrig was part of that, finishing third on the team in tackles. But what really caught my eye about his performance was the dominant block destruction on the play below. woah pic.twitter.com/UIgEZxbipA — Coach Dan Casey (@CoachDanCasey) November 22, 2026 Marcus Epps Score: 19-16 Eagles win Stats: 8 tackles, 1 TFL This week’s former Raider check-in is paying extra attention to the Raiders’ 2023 safety duo. Epps hasn’t done much since leaving Las Vegas and is more of a special teamer in Philadelphia this season. However, he received more playing time this week and made the most of it, ranking second on the Eagles in tackles. Also, all eight tackles were solos as the Birds got a much-needed win over their in-state rivals, the Pittsburgh Steelers. That win also helped the Raiders’ playoff odds (slightly) .
